Badges on edges and vulnerability markers on nodes add detail; **Hide blast radius** returns to the incident graph. Use the ungroup toggle to analyse one node in a group.
**Prerequisites:** onboarded Sentinel data lake and **Exposure management (read)** permission or higher.
**Limits to understand:** paths are *possible*, not guaranteed; only known attack vectors are modelled; results are scoped by your RBAC; calculations go up to seven hops (lower for some environments); data freshness lags.
Quality depends on data: if critical assets are not classified in Microsoft Security Exposure Management, the view under-represents risk.

terms.d: Potential impact of a compromised entity: paths it could take to reach critical assets.
An asset classified in Exposure Management as high value, used as a target in path calculations.
Unified RBAC permission required to see blast radius and graph data.

lessons.trap: Blast radius shows potential paths, not proof an attacker took them; and poor results usually mean critical assets were never classified.
lessons.example: During a token-theft incident, the analyst views the blast radius of the compromised user and sees a path to a SQL server, so they reset the user and contain the intermediate VM.

lessons.title: Entity relationships with Microsoft Sentinel graph
lessons.short: Microsoft Sentinel graph models users, devices, resources and activity as nodes and edges. It powers blast radius, the hunting graph and Exposure Management attack paths; you can query relationships with KQL graph operators or build custom graphs queried with GQL.
lessons.deep:
**Microsoft Sentinel graph** is the graph analytics layer of the Sentinel platform. Onboarding the Sentinel data lake enables it, and the hunting graph and blast radius are auto-provisioned in the Defender portal. Other consumers: attack paths in Security Exposure Management and Defender for Cloud, and data risk graphs in Microsoft Purview.
**KQL over the exposure graph:** the `ExposureGraphNodes` (NodeId, NodeLabel, NodeName, Categories, NodeProperties) and `ExposureGraphEdges` (SourceNodeId, TargetNodeId, EdgeLabel) tables can be turned into a graph:
`ExposureGraphEdges | make-graph SourceNodeId --> TargetNodeId with ExposureGraphNodes on NodeId | graph-match (A)-[e]->(B) where ... project ...`
Variable-length paths use `[e*1..3]`.
**Custom graphs (preview):** authored in Jupyter notebooks in the Microsoft Sentinel VS Code extension from data lake and third-party data, materialised with a graph job (on-demand graphs are kept 30 days; scheduled jobs rebuild on a refresh schedule) and queried with **GQL** on the **Graphs** page in the Defender portal. Billed on the Sentinel graph meter.
**AI access:** the Sentinel MCP server exposes graph tools such as `find_blastradius` and `find_walkable_paths`.

terms.d: KQL operator that builds a graph from an edges table, optionally joined to a nodes table.
KQL operator that finds patterns of nodes and edges in a graph built by make-graph.
Graph Query Language, used to query Sentinel custom graphs.

lessons.trap: Don't confuse the languages: exposure graph tables use KQL make-graph/graph-match, custom graphs use GQL.
lessons.example: A hunter uses graph-match over ExposureGraphEdges to list identities that can authenticate to more than one critical device.

lessons.title: Creating and running Sentinel hunting queries
lessons.short: Microsoft Sentinel > Threat management > Hunting lists built-in queries from Content hub solutions plus your custom ones, grouped by MITRE ATT&CK tactic. Run all or selected queries, then use Results and Results delta to spot what changed.
lessons.deep:
Hunting in Microsoft Sentinel is found at **Microsoft Sentinel > Threat management > Hunting** in the Defender portal (Azure portal: Threat management > Hunting; the Azure portal experience retires after March 31, 2027).
**Queries tab:** queries installed from **Content hub** solutions plus custom ones. Each shows description, data source, MITRE tactics and techniques, Results and **Results delta** (last 24 hours compared with the 24 to 48 hours before) and Results delta percentage. *N/A* means the required data source isn't connected.
**Run:** **Run all queries** or **Run selected queries**; favourited queries run automatically when the page opens. Results open in the Logs experience.
**Create:** Queries tab > **New query**; give a name, description, KQL, **entity mappings** (entity type, identifier, column) and **MITRE ATT&CK** tactic, technique and sub-technique, then **Create**.
**Change:** only custom-source queries can be edited; Content hub queries are **cloned** first. Right-click a query to run, edit, clone, delete or **Create analytics rule** when it is worth automating.
The MITRE ATT&CK page can also filter to techniques that have hunting queries. Microsoft recommends running relevant hunts at least weekly.

terms.d: Change in a hunting query's result count between the last 24 hours and the previous 24 to 48 hours.
Sentinel catalogue of solutions that install hunting queries, analytics rules, workbooks and more.
Mapping of query columns to entity types (Account, Host, IP...) so results link to entities.

lessons.trap: Built-in queries can't be edited in place; you clone them. And N/A means no data source, not zero results.
lessons.example: The SOC sorts by Results delta on Monday and sees a spike in a 'rare process as service' query, so it bookmarks the rows for investigation.

lessons.title: Monitoring hunts: bookmarks, hunts and follow-up
lessons.short: Bookmarks save interesting result rows with their query and time range in the HuntingBookmark table. Hunts group queries, bookmarks and entities around a hypothesis. Livestream is retired; use analytics rules or KQL jobs for ongoing monitoring.
lessons.deep:
**Bookmarks:** select rows in hunting results and choose **Add bookmark**. You can name it, map entities, set MITRE tactics/techniques, and add tags and notes. A bookmark keeps the rows, the KQL and the time range. Bookmarks are stored in the **HuntingBookmark** table, can open the investigation graph, and can create or be added to incidents. Bookmarks are not available in Defender advanced hunting.
**Hunts (preview):** the Hunts tab tracks a hypothesis-driven hunt end to end. Create a **New Hunt** or create one from selected queries (they are cloned into the hunt, so edits don't affect other hunts or the workspace). Each hunt has **Queries, Bookmarks and Entities** tabs, a hypothesis state and a status; the page shows metrics such as validated hypotheses, new incidents and new analytics rules. From the Entities tab you can open UEBA pages, add IPs to threat intelligence or run playbooks.
**Ongoing monitoring:** Sentinel livestream is no longer available. To keep watching a pattern, convert the query to an **analytics rule** (or NRT rule), or schedule a **KQL job** on the data lake, and use playbooks for notifications.

terms.d: Saved hunting result rows with query, time range, entities, tags and notes.
Log Analytics table where Sentinel bookmarks are stored.
Sentinel object tracking a hypothesis with its own cloned queries, bookmarks and entities.

lessons.trap: Livestream answers are outdated; for continuous monitoring choose an analytics rule or KQL job.
lessons.example: A hunter creates a hunt 'OAuth consent abuse', clones three queries into it, bookmarks two suspicious consents and promotes one bookmark to an incident.

lessons.title: KQL jobs in the Sentinel data lake
lessons.short: A KQL job is a one-time or scheduled KQL query over the Microsoft Sentinel data lake that writes results to a table: new analytics-tier tables get the _KQL_CL suffix, data lake tables get _KQL. Up to 5 jobs run concurrently per tenant.
lessons.deep:
The **Microsoft Sentinel data lake** stores large volumes of logs cheaply (up to 12 years). Interactive queries run in **Data lake exploration > KQL queries**; **KQL jobs** run them as background work and save the output.
**Create:** Microsoft Sentinel > Data lake exploration > **Jobs > Create job** (or Create job from the query editor, or from one of the built-in templates). Steps: name and description; destination workspace and table (new or existing); prepare the query and select source workspaces; choose **One time** or **Scheduled** (by minute, hourly, daily, weekly, monthly; start at least 30 minutes after creation); review and submit.
**Destinations:** analytics tier (new table suffix `_KQL_CL`, or append to an existing table with a matching schema, otherwise the job fails) or data lake tier System tables (suffix `_KQL`). Federated tables can't be destinations.
**Limits:** 5 concurrent executions per tenant (extra runs are rejected, not queued), 1-hour timeout, 100 enabled jobs, one output table per job.
**Unsupported:** `adx()`, `arg()`, `externaldata()`, `ingestion_time()` and user-defined functions.
**Latency:** new data can take up to 15 minutes to be queryable, so scheduled jobs offset the end time, e.g. `let endTime = now() - 15m;`.
Creating new analytics tables requires the data lake managed identity (msg-resources-<guid>) to hold Log Analytics Contributor.

terms.d: One-time or scheduled KQL query on the data lake that writes results to a table.
Suffix of a new analytics-tier table created by a KQL job.
Low-cost long-term Sentinel storage queried by KQL jobs, notebooks and data lake exploration.

lessons.trap: Suffixes are tested: _KQL_CL (KQL job, analytics), _SPRK_CL (notebook, analytics), _CL (summary rule or custom log).
lessons.example: A daily KQL job matches 90 days of firewall logs in the lake against new threat indicators and promotes matches to IOCMatches_KQL_CL for an analytics rule.

lessons.title: Summary rules and summary tables
lessons.short: Summary rules run a KQL aggregation on a schedule (bin sizes 20 minutes to 24 hours) and write the results to a custom _CL table on the Analytics plan. They make high-volume or low-cost-tier data fast and cheap to query and alert on.
lessons.deep:
Raw logs such as firewall or proxy events are often kept on the Basic or Auxiliary (data lake) plan because they are huge. **Summary rules** aggregate that data in the background and store the much smaller result in a custom table with the **Analytics** plan, where hunting queries, workbooks and analytics rules run quickly.
**Create:** Microsoft Sentinel > Configuration > **Summary rules > + Create**; name, description, destination table (`<name>_CL`, new or existing); optionally enable **SummaryLogs** diagnostic settings for run history; enter the KQL and preview results; set scheduling (how often, optional delay in minutes, start time). Content hub has summary rule templates (Templates tab).
**Rules of the query:** bin size `binSize` is 20, 30, 60, 120, 180, 360, 720 or 1440 minutes; delay up to 1440 minutes. Don't add a time filter: the bin defines the range. No `workspaces()`, `app()`, `resource()`, `adx()`, `arg()`, user-defined functions or `union *`. Max 100 active rules per workspace.
Result rows carry `_RuleName`, `_BinSize`, `_BinStartTime` and `_RuleLastModifiedTime`. Query the destination like any custom table.
**Role:** Microsoft Sentinel Contributor.

terms.d: Scheduled aggregation query that writes results to a custom Analytics-plan table.
Aggregation interval of a summary rule, 20 to 1440 minutes.
Column added to summary results showing the start of the aggregation bin.

lessons.trap: Summary rules aggregate recent data on a schedule; they can't backfill history (that's a KQL job), and adding a TimeGenerated filter is wrong.
lessons.example: An hourly summary rule counts CommonSecurityLog connections by source and destination IP into NetSummary_CL; an analytics rule then joins that table to threat intelligence.

lessons.title: Hunting with Jupyter notebooks on the data lake
lessons.short: Data lake notebooks run in Visual Studio Code with the Microsoft Sentinel extension, using PySpark on Small, Medium or Large pools. The MicrosoftSentinelProvider class reads tables (read_table) and writes results (save_as_table) to _SPRK lake or _SPRK_CL analytics tables.
lessons.deep:
Notebooks suit hunts that need code: machine learning, baselines, long timelines, custom graphs.
**Setup:** install VS Code, add the **Microsoft Sentinel** extension (optionally GitHub Copilot), sign in. The pane lists **Lake tables** and **Jobs**. Select the **Microsoft Sentinel** kernel and a pool: **Small** (testing, light work), **Medium** (ETL with joins, model training), **Large** (deep learning, big shuffles). A session takes a few minutes to start; the default session timeout is 30 minutes.
**Code:**
`from sentinel_lake.providers import MicrosoftSentinelProvider`
`data_provider = MicrosoftSentinelProvider(spark)`
`df = data_provider.read_table('SigninLogs', 'MyWorkspace')`
Other methods: `list_databases()`, `list_tables()`, `save_as_table(df, name, database, write_options)`, `delete_table()` (lake `_SPRK` tables only).
**Writing:** `_SPRK` suffix for the lake tier, `_SPRK_CL` for the analytics tier. Mode `append` is the default; `overwrite` works only in the lake tier.
**Jobs:** notebooks can be scheduled (and parameterised) as notebook jobs: 8-hour timeout, 3 concurrent jobs (others queue).
**Limits:** Python only; Azure Synapse libraries 3.4 plus the Sentinel provider, no pip installs; 100,000-row display limit.
The older Azure ML-based Sentinel notebooks with MSTICPy query the analytics workspace rather than the lake.

terms.d: PySpark class for listing, reading, writing and deleting data lake and analytics tables.
Required suffix when a notebook writes an analytics-tier table.
Compute size (Small, Medium, Large) chosen when selecting the Microsoft Sentinel kernel.

lessons.trap: Don't pick 'overwrite' for an analytics-tier write or pip-installing a library; both are unsupported.
lessons.example: A hunter reads 180 days of SigninLogs into a DataFrame, scores impossible-travel per user on a Medium pool, and appends the top risks to RiskySignins_SPRK_CL.

lessons.title: Connecting to the Microsoft Sentinel MCP server
lessons.short: The Microsoft Sentinel MCP server is a fully hosted Model Context Protocol endpoint that lets AI clients (VS Code agent mode, Security Copilot, Copilot Studio, Microsoft Foundry) search tables, run KQL on the data lake and analyse entities in natural language. It requires at least Security Reader.
lessons.deep:
**Model Context Protocol (MCP)** is an open standard that lets an AI host (for example VS Code) call tools exposed by a server. Microsoft hosts the Sentinel MCP server, so nothing is deployed; identity uses Microsoft Entra.
**Collections and URLs:**
- Data exploration: `https://sentinel.microsoft.com/mcp/data-exploration`
- Triage: `https://sentinel.microsoft.com/mcp/triage`
- Security Copilot agent creation: `https://sentinel.microsoft.com/mcp/security-copilot-agent-creation`
**Data exploration tools:** `list_sentinel_workspaces` (run first to get workspace IDs), `search_tables` (find relevant tables and schemas from keywords), `query_lake` (run a KQL query on the lake), `analyze_user_entity` / `analyze_url_entity` with `get_entity_analysis` (AI verdicts; consume SCUs, need Security Copilot Contributor; user analysis max 7 days and Entra users only), plus preview graph tools such as `find_blastradius`, `find_walkable_paths` and `find_exposure_perimeter`.
**Connect in VS Code:** Ctrl+Shift+P > **MCP: Add Server** > **HTTP** transport > paste the collection URL > give a server ID and scope > sign in with at least **Security Reader** > open Chat in **Agent mode** and confirm tools under Configure Tools.
Most tools require the Sentinel data lake to be onboarded.

terms.d: Model Context Protocol: standard for AI hosts to call tools exposed by servers.
Sentinel MCP tool that runs a KQL query against a data lake workspace.
Scenario-based group of Sentinel MCP tools exposed at its own URL.

lessons.trap: Entity analyzer tools need Security Copilot Contributor because they use SCUs; basic tools need only Security Reader.
lessons.example: From VS Code agent mode, an analyst asks 'find sign-in failures in the last 24 hours'; the agent calls search_tables, then query_lake, and summarises the result.

questions.stem: Where in the Microsoft Defender portal do you create a rule that emails the SOC when a new high-severity incident is created?
options: Settings > Microsoft Defender XDR > Alert tuning
Settings > Microsoft Defender XDR > Email notifications > Incidents
questions.explain: Incident email rules are on the Incidents tab of Settings > Microsoft Defender XDR > Email notifications. Advanced features are endpoint toggles, Alert tuning suppresses alerts, and Sentinel automation rules handle incident actions, not Defender email notifications.

questions.stem: Your tenant uses RBAC with device groups. An analyst whose role covers only the 'EU-Servers' device group creates an incident notification rule. What applies?
options: The rule covers all device groups because email notifications are tenant-wide
Device group scope applies only to Threat analytics notification rules
Device group scope can be set only by a Global Administrator
The analyst can only create, edit and receive notifications for device groups they can manage
questions.explain: With RBAC, users can only manage and receive notifications for device groups they're allowed to manage. Notifications are not automatically tenant-wide, scoping isn't Global-Admin-only, and device group scope is an incident/action setting, not a threat analytics one.

questions.stem: The SOC lead wants exactly one email per incident, only for High severity incidents, containing a link that opens the correct tenant. Which incident notification settings should you configure? Select THREE.
options: Send only one notification per incident
questions.explain: Severity High, one notification per incident, and the tenant-specific portal link meet all three needs. Action status belongs to action notification rules, and Content analysis is an automation uploads setting.

questions.stem: For each statement about Defender XDR email notifications, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Recipients added to an incident notification rule also receive emails for incidents that occurred before they were added.
An action notification rule can be limited to manual actions, automated actions, or both.
A Threat analytics notification rule can be limited to reports with a specific tag, such as ransomware.

questions.explain: Recipients only get notifications for incidents after they are added. Action rules filter by action source (manual/automated). Threat analytics rules can send for all reports or only filtered types/tags.

questions.stem: Which alert tuning action suppresses a Defender for Endpoint alert so that no incident is created, while still keeping the alert data in the AlertInfo and AlertEvidence tables?
questions.explain: Hide alert suppresses the alert (Defender for Endpoint only) and prevents incident creation, but data stays in AlertInfo/AlertEvidence. Resolve alert creates and auto-resolves it. Set as behavior converts signals into behaviors. Classifying is a manual triage step, not a tuning action.

questions.case: Contoso runs an authorised vulnerability scanner, scan.exe, every night from server SCAN01. Each run raises several Defender for Endpoint 'suspicious process' alerts that analysts close by hand every morning. Security wants the noise gone without weakening detection of the same behaviour from any other process or device.
questions.stem: What should you do?
options: Create an alert tuning rule with conditions on scan.exe and SCAN01 and a Resolve alert action
Add the scanner's folder to automation folder exclusions
Set SCAN01's device group to No automated response
Turn on 'Automatically resolve alerts' in advanced features
questions.explain: A narrowly scoped alert tuning rule handles this known benign activity only. Folder exclusions only affect automated investigation, No automated response stops remediation not alerts, and auto-resolve applies tenant-wide to remediated/no-threat alerts, not this scanner.

questions.stem: For each statement about alert tuning in Defender XDR, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Conditions in an alert tuning rule can be combined with AND and OR logic.
Microsoft's built-in alert tuning rules also apply to custom detection rules.
Alert tuning was previously called alert suppression.

questions.explain: Rules support AND/OR and grouping. Built-in tuning rules don't apply to custom detection rules or Custom TI. The feature was renamed from alert suppression to alert tuning.

questions.case: Fabrikam deployed the Security Copilot Phishing Triage Agent. Users report suspicious emails with the Report button, but the agent never classifies those alerts. The alerts appear as resolved in the queue almost immediately after they are created.
questions.stem: What is the most likely cause?
options: Restrict correlation to within scoped device groups is turned on
Automatic attack disruption contained the reporting users' mailboxes
A built-in alert tuning rule auto-resolves user-reported phishing alerts
The incident notification rule excludes Low severity alerts
questions.explain: The built-in 'Auto-Resolve - Email reported by user as malware or phish' tuning rule resolves these alerts, so the agent doesn't classify them; disable it and any similar custom rules. Correlation scoping, attack disruption and email notification rules don't resolve alerts.

questions.stem: Alerts from one Microsoft Sentinel analytics rule keep being merged by Defender XDR into large multi-stage incidents. You want that rule's alerts grouped only by the rule's own settings. What should you do?
options: Set Incident correlation to Disabled in the rule's Incident settings
Turn off alert grouping in the analytics rule
Create an alert tuning rule with the Hide alert action
Turn on 'Restrict correlation to within scoped device groups'
questions.explain: Setting Incident correlation to Disabled adds #DONT_CORR# to the description so the rule bypasses the correlation engine. Alert grouping is Sentinel's own grouping, Hide alert suppresses alerts entirely (and only for MDE), and the device-group setting affects Defender for Endpoint correlation.

questions.stem: Which conditions prevent Defender XDR from automatically merging two related incidents? Select THREE.
options: The incidents share the same user entity
One of the incidents is closed
The incidents are assigned to different analysts
The incidents were raised by different detection sources
questions.explain: Closed incidents, different assignees and different classifications/determinations block automatic merging. Shared entities and multiple detection sources are reasons to merge, not blockers.

questions.stem: Hidden alerts are still stored in the hunting tables. Complete the advanced hunting query so it returns each alert together with its file evidence.
questions.code:
AlertInfo
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| join kind=inner (AlertEvidence | where EntityType == "File") on ____
| project Timestamp, Title, Severity, FileName, SHA256
questions.explain: AlertInfo and AlertEvidence share the AlertId column, the documented join key. AlertInfo has no DeviceId or IncidentId columns, and Title isn't a key for joining evidence.

questions.stem: Your devices use a third-party antivirus, so Microsoft Defender Antivirus runs in passive mode. Which advanced feature lets Defender for Endpoint still block malicious artifacts it detects?
questions.explain: EDR in block mode blocks malicious artifacts even when Defender Antivirus is passive. Tamper protection locks settings, Allow or block file needs Defender AV active, and auto-resolve only changes alert status.

questions.case: A global company has local SOC teams in each region, each scoped by RBAC to its own device groups. Regional analysts complain that incidents contain alerts from devices in other regions that they can't open.
questions.stem: Which Defender for Endpoint advanced feature addresses this?
options: Restrict correlation to within scoped device groups
questions.explain: Restricting correlation to scoped device groups keeps alerts from different device groups out of the same incident (for future correlations). The other features affect inventory, user display and unmanaged device discovery.

questions.stem: You turn on the 'Allow or block file' advanced feature so you can block a file hash with an indicator. What must be true on the devices for blocking to work? Select TWO.
options: Device discovery is set to Standard discovery
Microsoft Defender Antivirus is the active antimalware solution
questions.explain: Allow or block file requires Defender Antivirus in active mode and cloud-based protection. Device discovery, live response and web content filtering are unrelated to file indicators.

questions.stem: For each statement about Defender for Endpoint advanced features, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Live response for servers is a separate setting from Live response.
Download quarantined files is turned on by default.
Allow unsigned script execution in live response must be on before any script, signed or unsigned, can run in a live response session.

questions.explain: Server live response has its own toggle, and Download quarantined files is on by default. The unsigned-script toggle is only needed for unsigned scripts; signed scripts run without it.

questions.stem: What is the maximum number of indicators of compromise a single Defender for Endpoint tenant can hold?
questions.explain: Defender for Endpoint supports 15,000 indicators per tenant, and the limit can't be increased. The other numbers are not the documented limit.

questions.stem: HR wants users who browse to a gambling domain to see a warning but still be able to continue if they have a business reason. Which indicator action should you use?
questions.explain: Warn shows a bypassable warning. Audit only raises an alert with no user prompt, Block execution stops access entirely, and Block and remediate isn't available for URL/domain indicators.

questions.stem: For each statement about Defender for Endpoint indicators, select Yes if true.

statements.s: An IP address indicator can specify a CIDR range such as 10.0.0.0/24.
Indicators aren't supported when Microsoft Defender Antivirus is in passive mode.
A domain indicator for contoso.com also matches its subdomains.

questions.explain: IP indicators need full single addresses; wildcards and ranges aren't supported. Indicators require Defender Antivirus not in passive mode. A domain indicator matches subdomains.

questions.stem: You add D:\BuildOutput as an automation folder exclusion in Defender for Endpoint. What is the effect?
options: Microsoft Defender Antivirus stops scanning the folder
Automated investigation skips the folder, but antivirus still scans it
ASR rules no longer evaluate processes started from the folder
Files in the folder are always uploaded for content analysis
questions.explain: Automation folder exclusions affect only automated investigation and remediation; antivirus scanning continues. They aren't AV or ASR exclusions, and uploads are controlled by the Automation uploads setting.

questions.stem: Which Defender for Endpoint setting lets you list file extensions that are sent to the cloud for extra inspection during automated investigation?
questions.explain: Automation uploads with Content analysis on sends the listed extensions for cloud inspection. Custom data collection sends telemetry to Sentinel, folder exclusions skip folders, and indicators allow or block entities.

questions.stem: Where are events gathered by Defender for Endpoint custom data collection rules stored for analysis?
options: In a connected Microsoft Sentinel workspace
Only in the 30-day advanced hunting store
In an Azure Storage account through the streaming API
questions.explain: Custom data collection routes matching events to the connected Sentinel workspace in DeviceCustom* tables. It doesn't use the default advanced hunting store, Purview Audit, or the streaming API.

questions.stem: A custom data collection rule captures powershell.exe process launches on admin workstations. Complete the Sentinel query to review the events from the last day that the rule collected.
questions.code:
____
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where FileName =~ "powershell.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, ProcessCommandLine, RuleName
questions.explain: Process events from custom collection rules land in DeviceCustomProcessEvents, which has the RuleName column. DeviceProcessEvents is default telemetry without RuleName, DeviceCustomNetworkEvents holds connections, and SecurityEvent is Windows event log data.

questions.stem: You plan to create custom data collection rules in Defender for Endpoint. Which prerequisites must be in place? Select THREE.
options: Manual device tags added on each device page
Dynamic tags configured in Asset rule management
questions.explain: You need Plan 2, a connected Sentinel workspace, and dynamic tags from Asset rule management to target devices. Manual tags aren't supported, and Purview Audit isn't involved.

questions.stem: A rule collecting file events on a busy file server reaches its limit by mid-afternoon. For each statement, select Yes if true.

statements.s: The rule stops collecting on that device after 75,000 events within a 24-hour rolling window.
All other custom collection rules on the same device also stop until the window resets.
Data collected by custom rules is billed at the Sentinel ingestion rates you pay.

questions.explain: Each rule is capped at 75,000 events per device per rolling 24 hours; only that rule pauses while others continue. The feature is included in Plan 2, but Sentinel ingestion is billed.

questions.case: Litware onboarded 300 Windows servers to Defender for Endpoint. They aren't enrolled in Intune but security settings management is enabled. You create an ASR rules policy on the Endpoint security policies page of the Defender portal.
questions.stem: How should you assign the policy?
options: To Microsoft Entra user groups of the server administrators
To Intune scope tags for the servers
To Microsoft Entra security groups that contain the server devices
To the Defender for Endpoint 'Servers' device group in Settings > Endpoints
questions.explain: Devices managed only by security settings management must be targeted with Entra groups containing the devices; user targeting isn't supported. Scope tags aren't available in the Defender wizard, and Defender device groups control RBAC/automation, not policy assignment.

questions.stem: You create an endpoint security policy in the Microsoft Defender portal. Put the steps in order.
options: Select Create new policy, then choose the platform and template
Enter a unique name on the Basics page
Configure the settings on Configuration settings
Add include or exclude groups on Assignments
questions.explain: The wizard runs platform/template selection, Basics, Configuration settings, Assignments, then Review + create.

questions.stem: Which attack surface reduction rule mode blocks the behaviour but lets the user choose to unblock it?
questions.explain: Warn mode blocks with a prompt the user can bypass. Audit only logs, Block blocks with no bypass, and Not configured leaves the rule off.

questions.stem: Complete the advanced hunting query so it returns all audited and blocked ASR rule events from the last 7 days.
questions.code:
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType ____ "Asr"
| summarize Events = count() by ActionType, DeviceName
questions.explain: ASR action types begin with 'Asr' (e.g. AsrLsassCredentialTheftBlocked), so startswith matches them all. == matches only the literal 'Asr', endswith matches nothing, and !contains excludes them.

questions.stem: You want to test the LSASS credential-theft ASR rule on one device without blocking anything. Complete the PowerShell command.
questions.code: Add-MpPreference -AttackSurfaceReductionRules_Ids 9e6c4e1f-7d60-472f-ba1a-a39ef669e4b2 -AttackSurfaceReductionRules_Actions ____
questions.explain: 2 is Audit mode, which logs without blocking. 1 is Block, 6 is Warn (not supported by the LSASS rule), and 0 disables the rule.

questions.stem: For each statement about attack surface reduction rules, select Yes if true.

statements.s: The 'Block credential stealing from the Windows local security authority subsystem' rule supports Warn mode.
If you suspect a false positive, Microsoft recommends switching the rule to Audit mode before adding an exclusion.
ASR exclusions can be applied globally or to an individual rule.

questions.explain: The LSASS rule doesn't support Warn. Microsoft advises testing in Audit before excluding because exclusions let files run unreported. Both global and per-rule exclusions exist.

questions.stem: After September 1, 2026, AIR can no longer be triggered manually for Defender for Endpoint. What does Microsoft recommend for an on-demand investigation of a suspicious device?
options: Run a full Microsoft Defender Antivirus scan
Restrict app execution on the device
questions.explain: Microsoft says full antivirus scans replace manual AIR investigations, because AIR now runs inside default antivirus protection. The other actions are useful response tools but aren't the stated replacement.

questions.stem: Which verdicts can an automated investigation assign to a piece of evidence? Select THREE.
questions.explain: AIR verdicts are Malicious, Suspicious and No threats found. Informational is an alert severity and Benign positive is an incident/alert classification set by analysts.

questions.stem: For each statement about the Action center, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Email remediation actions identified by automated investigation wait for approval on the Pending tab.
Some completed actions, such as Isolate device, can be undone from the History tab.
The History tab lists only actions from automated investigations, not live response commands.

questions.explain: Email remediation always needs approval. Isolate device and Restrict code execution can be undone in History. History also records manual actions, live response commands and AV remediations.

questions.case: Your tenant uses Microsoft Defender XDR Unified RBAC. An automated investigation found a phishing campaign and proposed soft-deleting the messages from 60 mailboxes. A tier-2 analyst with a custom role containing Security data basics (read) and Response (manage) can see the pending action but can't approve it.
questions.stem: Which permission should you add to the analyst's custom role?
questions.explain: Approving email remediation needs Email & collaboration advanced actions (manage). Response (manage) covers device actions. Detection tuning manages custom detections and tuning, and the other two govern settings and roles.

questions.stem: In the incident queue, how can you quickly identify incidents where automatic attack disruption took action?
options: Their status is set to Resolved
Their severity is raised to High
questions.explain: Disrupted incidents carry the Attack Disruption tag (and a yellow banner on the incident page). Redirected marks merged source incidents; status and severity don't identify disruption.

questions.stem: Which response actions can automatic attack disruption take? Select THREE.
options: Disable the user in Active Directory through Defender for Identity
questions.explain: Disruption can contain devices, disable AD users via the Defender for Identity sensor, and revoke sessions. It doesn't wipe devices or delete mailboxes; actions are containment and reversible.

questions.case: Northwind's break-glass Global Administrator account is used only in emergencies from unusual locations. The CISO worries automatic attack disruption could disable it during a real outage. Microsoft Defender for Identity and Defender for Endpoint are deployed, and Unified RBAC is enabled.
questions.stem: What should you configure so the account is never automatically disabled, while disruption still protects all other accounts?
options: Add a user exclusion on the Identities tab of Settings > Microsoft Defender XDR > Automated response
Exclude the account from all Conditional Access policies
Create an alert tuning rule that hides alerts involving the account
Open a support case titled 'Attack disruption opt-out'
questions.explain: A user exclusion in Automated response settings stops that account being automatically disabled. Conditional Access exclusions don't affect disruption, hiding alerts weakens detection, and the support-case opt-out turns off automated disruption actions for the whole tenant.

questions.stem: After an attack disruption incident, you want to review on-premises accounts that were disabled. Complete the advanced hunting query.
questions.code:
IdentityDirectoryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where ActionType == ____
| project Timestamp, TargetAccountUpn, ActionType
questions.explain: Microsoft's guidance is to query IdentityDirectoryEvents for ActionType == "Account disabled" to review disable events. LogonFailed belongs to logon tables, and the other two values describe password changes and replication, not disabling.

questions.stem: For each statement about automatic attack disruption prerequisites, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Device discovery must be set to Standard discovery for the automatic Contain device action.
Attack disruption works only when Microsoft Defender Antivirus is in active mode.
The Defender for Cloud Apps Microsoft 365 connector should be configured with all checkboxes selected.

questions.explain: Contain device needs Standard discovery, and the Microsoft 365 app connector must be fully configured. Disruption works whatever the antivirus state: active, passive or EDR block mode.

questions.stem: Device SRV-DE-01 matches the rules of 'All-Servers' (rank 3) and 'DE-Servers' (rank 1). Which device group is it in?
options: All-Servers, because the broader rule wins
questions.explain: A device is added only to the highest-ranked group it matches; rank 1 is highest, so it joins DE-Servers. Devices are never in two groups, and Ungrouped is only for devices that match no group.

questions.stem: Which properties can a Defender for Endpoint device group matching rule use? Select THREE.
questions.explain: Matching rules use device name, domain, tags and OS platform. Risk level and logged-on user aren't matching-rule properties.

questions.stem: You want Windows servers to join a device group whose rule matches the tag 'Finance-Servers'. Complete the registry command that sets the device tag.
questions.code: reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Advanced Threat Protection\DeviceTagging" /v ____ /t REG_SZ /d "Finance-Servers" /f
questions.explain: The registry tag is a REG_SZ value named Group under the DeviceTagging key. Tag, MachineGroup and DeviceTag aren't the documented value name.

questions.case: Your tenant uses Microsoft Defender XDR Unified RBAC. Tier-1 analysts in Japan must view alerts and run basic live response, but only on devices in the 'JP-Workstations' device group. They must not upload or run scripts on devices.
questions.stem: What should you do?
options: Assign the Microsoft Entra Security Operator role to the analysts
Create a custom Unified RBAC role with Security data basics (read) and Basic live response, scoped to the JP-Workstations device group
Create a custom role with Advanced live response, scoped to all devices
Assign Microsoft Sentinel Responder on the Sentinel resource group
questions.explain: A custom role with only the needed permissions, scoped to the device group, meets least privilege. Security Operator is tenant-wide, Advanced live response allows script upload/run, and Sentinel Responder governs Sentinel incidents, not device actions.

questions.stem: You create a new device group in Defender for Endpoint. Put the wizard steps in order.
options: General: enter the name and automation level
User access: assign Microsoft Entra user groups
questions.explain: The device group wizard runs General, Devices (matching rule), Preview devices, then User access.

questions.stem: Which automation level does Microsoft recommend for Defender for Endpoint device groups?
options: Semi - require approval for all folders
Semi - require approval for core folders remediation
questions.explain: Microsoft recommends Full - remediate threats automatically, and it is the default for tenants created on or after 16 August 2020. The Semi levels need approvals, and No automated response isn't recommended.

questions.stem: A device group is set to 'Semi - require approval for non-temp folders remediation'. Malicious files are found in C:\Users\amy\AppData\Local\Temp and C:\Program Data\App. What happens?
options: The Temp file is remediated automatically; the other waits for approval
The Temp file waits for approval; the other is remediated automatically
questions.explain: At this level only files in temporary folders are remediated automatically; anything outside temp folders needs approval in the Action center.

questions.stem: For each statement about automation levels, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Pending remediation actions that aren't approved time out after seven days.
'Core folders' refers to operating system directories such as \windows\*.
You can't change the automation level of the Ungrouped devices (default) group.

questions.explain: Pending actions time out after seven days, and core folders are OS directories. Ungrouped devices can't be deleted or re-ranked, but its automation level can be changed.

questions.stem: Which triggers can a Microsoft Sentinel automation rule use? Select THREE.
questions.explain: Automation rules trigger on incident created, incident updated and alert created. Watchlist changes and connector health aren't automation rule triggers; connector health is monitored with SentinelHealth.

questions.case: Rule 1 (order 1) lowers severity from Medium to Low for incidents from the 'Legacy VPN' analytics rule. Rule 2 (order 2) assigns incidents with severity Medium or higher to Tier-2. Both use the When incident is created trigger.
questions.stem: A new Medium incident is created by 'Legacy VPN'. What happens?
options: Both rules run at the same time, so the incident is Low and assigned to Tier-2
Rule 2 runs first because assignment actions have priority
Severity becomes Low and Rule 2 doesn't run because its condition is no longer met
Rule 2 evaluates the original Medium severity and assigns the incident
questions.explain: Rules run sequentially by order and evaluate the current state; after Rule 1 sets Low, Rule 2's Medium-or-higher condition is false. Rules never run in parallel, and no action type gets priority.

questions.stem: A red team exercise runs for one week and will generate many incidents from a known test account. You want those incidents closed automatically during the test only. What should you configure?
options: An automation rule that closes matching incidents, with an expiration date at the end of the test
A watchlist of the test account referenced in every analytics rule
A playbook with an alert trigger that deletes the alerts
Turn off all analytics rules for the week
questions.explain: Automation rules can close incidents with a reason and comment and expire automatically, which suits time-limited suppression. Editing every rule, deleting alerts or disabling detection would be heavy-handed or remove visibility.

questions.stem: Health monitoring is on in Microsoft Sentinel. Complete the query to list automation rule runs that didn't fully succeed in the last 24 hours.
questions.code:
SentinelHealth
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where OperationName == "Automation rule run"
| where Status ____ "Success"
| project TimeGenerated, SentinelResourceName, Status, Description
questions.explain: Status != "Success" returns Partial success and Failure runs. == returns only successes, startswith returns only successes, and has "Success" matches Success and Partial success but misses Failure.

questions.stem: You build a playbook that comments on and closes Sentinel incidents, using the logic app's system-assigned managed identity. Which role should the managed identity have on the Sentinel workspace?
questions.explain: Playbooks that update incidents need Microsoft Sentinel Responder (Reader is for playbooks that only receive incidents). Playbook Operator runs playbooks, and Logic App Contributor edits logic apps; neither grants incident updates.

questions.case: An engineer created a playbook in resource group RG-Playbooks. When building an automation rule in the Sentinel workspace (in RG-Sentinel), the playbook is greyed out and can't be selected. The engineer is Owner on both resource groups.
questions.stem: What should the engineer do?
options: Assign the engineer Microsoft Sentinel Playbook Operator
In Manage playbook permissions, grant Microsoft Sentinel permissions on RG-Playbooks
Recreate the playbook as a Logic Apps Standard workflow
Change the playbook trigger from incident to entity
questions.explain: Automation rules run playbooks through the Sentinel service account, which needs explicit permissions (Automation Contributor) on the playbook's resource group. User roles don't fix it, Standard doesn't help, and an entity trigger can't be called by automation rules.

questions.stem: For each statement about Microsoft Sentinel playbooks, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Logic Apps Standard playbooks can be created directly from Sentinel playbook templates.
A playbook that must reach resources through a private endpoint is a good fit for Logic Apps Standard.
An automation rule with an incident trigger can run only incident-trigger playbooks.

questions.explain: Templates support Consumption only; Standard workflows are built manually. Standard supports private endpoints and VNet integration. Incident-trigger automation rules run incident-trigger playbooks only.

questions.stem: You want a playbook to authenticate to Microsoft Sentinel with a managed identity. Put the steps in order.
options: Enable the system-assigned managed identity on the logic app
On the workspace, use Access control (IAM) to grant the identity a Sentinel role
In the Sentinel connector, select Connect with managed identity
Save and test the playbook against an incident
questions.explain: The identity must exist before it can get a role, and it needs the role before the connector connection using it will work; then test.

questions.stem: During a hunt, an analyst wants to run a playbook against a single IP address that isn't in any incident. Which playbook trigger supports this?
questions.explain: Entity-trigger playbooks run manually on an entity such as an IP, account or host, including from hunting. Incident and alert triggers need those objects, and a recurrence trigger is a schedule, not a Sentinel trigger.

questions.stem: Which is the least-privileged built-in role that lets a SOC analyst assign incidents and change their status in Microsoft Sentinel?
questions.explain: Responder adds incident management to Reader. Reader is view-only, Contributor adds rule and content management beyond what's needed, and Automation Contributor is for the Sentinel service account, not users.

questions.stem: A security engineer must install solutions from Content hub and create analytics rules. Which built-in role should you assign at the Sentinel resource group?
questions.explain: Microsoft Sentinel Contributor can manage Content hub and create/edit analytics rules. Responder only manages incidents, Log Analytics Contributor isn't Sentinel-specific, and Workbook Contributor only covers workbooks.

questions.case: Tier-1 SOC analysts must triage and close incidents in Microsoft Sentinel and manually run existing playbooks from incidents. They must not create or edit playbooks or analytics rules.
questions.stem: Which roles should you assign? Select TWO.
options: Microsoft Sentinel Responder on the Sentinel resource group
Logic App Contributor on the playbook resource group
Microsoft Sentinel Playbook Operator on the playbook resource group
Microsoft Sentinel Contributor on the Sentinel resource group
Microsoft Sentinel Automation Contributor on the playbook resource group
questions.explain: Microsoft's guidance for SOC analysts is Responder plus Playbook Operator. Logic App Contributor allows editing playbooks, Contributor allows editing rules, and Automation Contributor isn't for users.

questions.stem: For each statement about Microsoft Sentinel permissions, select Yes if true.

statements.s: A user with Microsoft Sentinel Responder also needs Workbook Contributor to save a new workbook.
The Microsoft Entra Security Reader role can run KQL jobs that write to Sentinel data lake tables.
Role assignments are cumulative, so a user with Reader and Contributor has Contributor permissions.

questions.explain: Reader/Responder need Workbook Contributor to create workbooks. Security Reader can read the data lake but writing needs Security Operator, Security Administrator or Global Administrator. Azure role assignments add up.

questions.case: A data engineer must schedule KQL jobs that read from the Sentinel data lake and write results into new tables. Your policy requires the least privileged Microsoft Entra role that meets the need.
questions.stem: Which Microsoft Entra role should you assign?
questions.explain: Security Operator can write to data lake tables and manage scheduled jobs, with fewer rights than Security Administrator. Security Reader and Global Reader are read-only for the data lake.

questions.stem: What is the maximum total retention for a Microsoft Sentinel table using the data lake tier?
questions.explain: Total retention, extended through the data lake tier, can reach 12 years. Two years is the analytics tier maximum, and 90 days is the included free analytics retention for Sentinel.

questions.case: Contoso ingests 400 GB per day of firewall traffic logs. They are rarely queried, aren't used by any analytics rule, but must be kept for one year for compliance and searched occasionally during investigations.
questions.stem: What is the most cost-effective configuration for the firewall table?
options: Data lake tier with 1-year total retention
Analytics tier with 30-day retention and a daily export to Azure Storage
Analytics tier with a 100 GB/day commitment tier
questions.explain: The data lake tier gives cheap long-term storage queried with KQL jobs, ideal for high-volume compliance logs not needed for detection. One-year analytics retention is expensive, exports add complexity, and a commitment tier doesn't reduce retention cost.

questions.stem: A table is moved from the Analytics tier to the Data lake tier. Which features can no longer use that table? Select THREE.
questions.explain: Data-lake-only tables can't feed analytics rules, workbooks, hunting queries or watchlists. They are queried with KQL jobs, summary rules and notebooks.

questions.stem: You manage table retention with the Azure CLI. Complete the command so SigninLogs keeps 180 days in the Analytics tier and two years in total.
questions.code: az monitor log-analytics workspace table update --resource-group rg-sentinel --workspace-name ws-sentinel --name SigninLogs --retention-time 180 ____ 730
questions.explain: --retention-time sets interactive (analytics) retention and --total-retention-time sets total retention including long-term storage. --plan changes the table plan, and the other two parameters don't exist on this command.

questions.stem: By default, how far back can you query Defender XDR advanced hunting tables such as DeviceProcessEvents?
questions.explain: Advanced hunting data is kept for 30 days in the XDR default tier. 180 days is Defender for Endpoint's portal data retention, and 90 days is Sentinel's included analytics retention.

questions.case: Investigations at Adatum often find attacker dwell times of five months. The SOC needs to hunt DeviceNetworkEvents back six months with KQL. Real-time detections on the older data aren't needed, and the budget is tight. Microsoft Sentinel is onboarded to the Defender portal.
questions.stem: What should you configure for DeviceNetworkEvents in Table management?
options: Leave the XDR default 30 days and export data with the streaming API
Data lake tier with total retention of 180 days
Basic logs plan with 180 days retention
questions.explain: Data lake tier keeps 30 days in advanced hunting at no extra cost and stores older data cheaply for KQL jobs, avoiding analytics ingestion charges. Analytics 180 days works but costs more; streaming adds infrastructure; Table management offers Analytics or Data lake tiers, not a Basic plan, for XDR tables.

questions.stem: A workbook has a time range parameter named TimeRange. Complete the query so it honours the time picker.
questions.code:
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated ____
| where ResultType != "0"
| summarize Failures = count() by UserPrincipalName
| top 10 by Failures
questions.explain: {TimeRange} expands into a complete clause such as > ago(1d). TimeRange without braces isn't substituted, and grain is the bin size for time-series, not a filter.

questions.stem: You want a customised copy of the Microsoft Entra sign-in logs workbook. Put the steps in order.
options: Install the Microsoft Entra solution from Content hub
Open Workbooks > Templates and select the workbook
Select Save to create a saved copy
Select View saved workbook, then Edit
questions.explain: The template comes from the Content hub solution; you save it to create your own resource, then open and edit the saved copy.

questions.stem: A SOC optimization threat-based recommendation for AiTM attacks says the required data sources are ingested, but the related detections are missing. What is the recommended action?
options: Turn on the relevant analytics rule templates
Move the tables to the Basic logs plan
questions.explain: When data exists but detections don't, SOC optimization recommends enabling analytics rule templates. Connecting data is for when rules exist but data is missing; changing plans is a data value action; dismissing ignores the gap.

questions.stem: For each statement about SOC optimization, select Yes if true.

statements.s: SOC optimization recommendations are recalculated every 24 hours.
Similar organizations recommendations can suggest custom tables used by other companies.
Using SOC optimization requires the workspace to be onboarded to the Defender portal.

questions.explain: Recommendations refresh every 24 hours and need a Defender-portal-onboarded workspace. Similar organizations recommendations exclude custom tables and connectors.

questions.stem: Complete the query that shows billable ingestion in GB per table over the last 30 days, so you can find the costliest tables.
questions.code:
Usage
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where IsBillable == true
| summarize BillableGB = ____ / 1000. by DataType
| sort by BillableGB desc
questions.explain: Quantity is in MB, so sum(Quantity) / 1000. gives GB. count() returns row counts, _BilledSize is in bytes (dividing by 1000 wouldn't give GB), and dcount counts distinct values.

questions.stem: Which data sources can you ingest into Microsoft Sentinel at no ingestion charge? Select THREE.
questions.explain: Azure Activity, Office 365 audit (OfficeActivity) and Defender security alerts (SecurityAlert/SecurityIncident) are free. Entra ID sign-in logs and CEF firewall data are billed.

questions.case: Tailspin ingests a steady 140 GB per day into the Sentinel analytics tier on pay-as-you-go. Finance asks for a lower predictable bill. Volume is expected to stay stable, but could drop if a planned migration to the data lake tier succeeds next quarter.
questions.stem: Which statement about moving to a commitment tier is correct?
options: Commitment tiers start at 500 GB/day, so Tailspin isn't eligible
You can raise or lower the commitment tier at any time with no restriction
Data above the commitment is rejected until the next day
Tailspin can select the 100 GB/day tier, and can lower a tier only once every 31 days
questions.explain: Commitment tiers begin at 100 GB/day; you can increase any time but decrease only once every 31 days. Usage above the tier is billed at the same effective rate, not rejected.

questions.stem: Which table should you query to find failed Microsoft Sentinel automation rule runs and playbook triggers?
questions.explain: SentinelHealth records 'Automation rule run' and 'Playbook was triggered' events with a Status. SentinelAudit records configuration changes, SecurityIncident holds incidents, and Usage holds ingestion volume.

questions.case: SOC optimization reports that table ProxyLogs_CL (40 GB/day) wasn't used by any analytics rule, hunting query or workbook in the last 30 days. Legal says the logs must be retained for 3 years in case of disputes.
questions.stem: What is the best response to the recommendation?
options: Stop ingestion and delete the table
Move the table to the data lake tier with 3-year total retention
Mark the recommendation as completed without changes
questions.explain: The data is needed for compliance but not detection, so cheap long-term data lake storage fits. Deleting breaks the legal requirement, marking complete fixes nothing, and analytics retention max is 2 years and costly.

questions.stem: Where do you normally install a Microsoft Sentinel data connector together with its related analytics rules and workbooks?
questions.explain: Connectors ship inside Content hub solutions, which also bring rules, workbooks and playbooks. The Workbooks gallery holds dashboards only. Defender for Cloud recommendations are posture findings, not a connector catalogue.

questions.stem: You must ingest Microsoft Entra ID sign-in logs into Microsoft Sentinel using the Microsoft Entra ID connector. Which TWO requirements apply? Select TWO.
options: A Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2 licence
An Azure Arc-enabled server running the Azure Monitor Agent
Security Administrator role (or equivalent) on the tenant
questions.explain: Sign-in logs need Entra ID P1 or P2 (audit logs work with any licence), and connecting needs Security Administrator or equivalent plus workspace write access. Arc/AMA and WEC are for server logs. TAXII is for threat intelligence.

questions.case: Contoso forwards Security log events from 600 servers to a Windows Event Collector with WEF. The AMA on the collector uses the Windows Forwarded Events connector. Several built-in Sentinel rules for Windows security events never fire, even though analysts can see the events in the workspace.
questions.stem: What is the most likely cause?
options: NRT rules cannot query on-premises data
The collector lacks the Monitoring Metrics Publisher role
The events are stored in WindowsEvent, but the built-in rules query SecurityEvent
The DCR uses the Minimal event set
questions.explain: Windows Forwarded Events writes to WindowsEvent even for Security-channel events. Many built-in rules query SecurityEvent, so they must be adapted or the Security Events via AMA connector used. Event sets belong to the Security Events connector. Monitoring Metrics Publisher is for the Logs Ingestion API.

questions.stem: For each statement about Windows data in Microsoft Sentinel, select Yes if true.

statements.s: The Windows Security Events via AMA connector writes to the SecurityEvent table.
Events forwarded from the Security log through WEF are written to SecurityEvent by the Windows Forwarded Events connector.
The Microsoft Defender XDR connector can stream DeviceProcessEvents into the workspace.

questions.explain: Security Events via AMA writes to SecurityEvent. Forwarded Events writes to WindowsEvent whatever the original channel. The Defender XDR connector can stream advanced hunting tables such as DeviceProcessEvents.

questions.stem: Which Windows security event set captures a full user audit trail, including sign-out events such as 4634, while reducing volume compared with collecting everything?
questions.explain: Common keeps a full user audit trail (logons, logoffs, group changes, Kerberos) at reduced volume. Minimal targets breach indicators and drops 4634, so it isn't a full trail. All is the unfiltered Security and AppLocker logs. Custom means your own XPath.

questions.stem: You plan to use Windows Security Events via AMA for 50 physical Windows servers in an on-premises datacenter. What must be in place before you add them to the data collection rule?
options: Log Analytics agent (MMA) on each server
Azure Arc Connected Machine agent on each server
questions.explain: Non-Azure machines must be Azure Arc-enabled before the AMA-based connector can target them. The DCR then installs the AMA. MMA is the retired legacy agent. WEC is only for the Forwarded Events connector. MDE onboarding is unrelated to AMA collection.

questions.stem: You create a Custom event set in a DCR to collect only successful and failed logons. Complete the XPath query.
questions.code: Security!*[System[(____)]]
questions.explain: AMA supports XPath 1.0, which uses = and the keyword 'or'. 'in ()' and '==/||' are KQL or C-style syntax and are invalid in XPath. 'and' would need an event to have both IDs at once, which never happens.

questions.stem: You are connecting Azure VMs with Windows Security Events via AMA. Put the steps in order.
options: Install the Windows Server Security Events solution from Content hub
Open the Windows Security Events via AMA connector page
Select + Add data collection rule and enter name, subscription and resource group
Add the target VMs on the Resources tab
Choose the event set on the Collect tab and create the rule
questions.explain: You install the solution, open its connector, start a DCR (Basics), pick resources (the AMA is deployed to them), choose All/Common/Minimal/Custom on Collect, then review and create.

questions.stem: Before adding a custom XPath query to a DCR, how can you check locally on a Windows server that the query is valid?
options: Run Test-NetConnection to the workspace endpoint
questions.explain: Get-WinEvent -LogName Security -FilterXPath tests the expression. An 'invalid query' error means bad syntax. wecutil qc configures an event collector, auditpol shows audit policy, and Test-NetConnection checks network reachability.

questions.stem: You configure source-initiated Windows Event Forwarding by Group Policy so clients forward their Security log. Which THREE client-side settings are required? Select THREE.
options: Add Network Service to the Event Log Readers group
Start the Windows Remote Management (WinRM) service
Configure target Subscription Manager with the collector URI
Enable the Windows Firewall rule for SMB on the collector
Install the Azure Monitor Agent on every client
questions.explain: Clients need the subscription manager URI, a running WinRM service, and Network Service in Event Log Readers to read the secured Security channel. A key WEF benefit is that only the collector needs the AMA. WEF uses WinRM, not SMB.

questions.stem: By default, which event log on a Windows Event Collector receives events from WEF subscriptions?
questions.explain: Subscriptions write into the ForwardedEvents log on the collector by default, and the Forwarded Events connector reads it. The collector's own Security and System logs hold its local events. The EventCollector operational channel logs the service's own status.

questions.case: Fabrikam has 8,000 domain-joined workstations. The CISO wants their Security events in Microsoft Sentinel without deploying or managing an agent on each workstation. A single on-premises server can be dedicated to collection.
questions.stem: Which design should you recommend?
options: Windows Security Events via AMA with a DCR targeting all workstations through Azure Arc
Syslog via AMA on a Linux forwarder receiving Windows events on port 514
Collector-initiated WEF with all 8,000 workstations listed individually on the collector
Source-initiated WEF via GPO to a WEC with the AMA and Azure Arc, using Windows Forwarded Events
questions.explain: Source-initiated WEF scales through GPO, and only the collector needs Arc plus the AMA. Collector-initiated suits small named sets and doesn't scale to thousands. A per-workstation DCR means 8,000 agents. Windows doesn't natively send its events as syslog.

questions.stem: For each statement about Windows Event Forwarding, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Collector-initiated subscriptions require the collector to be preconfigured with the list of source computers.
In an Active Directory domain, WEF traffic is authenticated and encrypted with Kerberos by default.
WEF can change audit policy on source computers to start generating missing events.

questions.explain: Collector-initiated (pull) uses a named source list. In a domain, Kerberos protects WEF by default. WEF is passive: it can't change audit policy or channel settings, so that must be done through GPO or other tools.

questions.stem: You run the Forwarder_AMA_installer.py script on a Linux log forwarder. Which port does it configure the syslog daemon to listen on for remote messages?
questions.explain: The script configures rsyslog or syslog-ng and opens port 514 for both TCP and UDP. 6514 is syslog over TLS by convention but isn't what the script opens. 443 is the AMA's outbound port to Azure. 5986 is WinRM over HTTPS.

questions.stem: In a Syslog via AMA data collection rule you set the auth facility to LOG_ERR. Which messages from that facility are collected?
options: LOG_ERR and all less severe levels down to LOG_DEBUG
questions.explain: The portal picks a minimum level. That level and every more severe level are collected. Collecting a single exact level, or levels below it, needs a DCR built through the API.

questions.stem: You are preparing an on-premises Ubuntu VM as a log forwarder for Syslog via AMA. Which TWO prerequisites must be met? Select TWO.
options: The Azure Arc Connected Machine agent is installed
The VM is joined to Microsoft Entra Domain Services
The Windows Event Collector service is configured
The VM hosts a TAXII server
questions.explain: A non-Azure forwarder needs the Arc Connected Machine agent so the AMA and DCR can target it, and it must run rsyslog or syslog-ng (plus Python 2.7 or 3). WEC is a Windows component. Domain join and TAXII are unrelated.

questions.case: A Syslog via AMA forwarder stops sending data to Sentinel after two weeks. Investigation shows the root file system is 100% full because rsyslog writes every received message to /var/log.
questions.stem: What should you do to prevent a recurrence?
options: Switch the DCR to the Minimal event set
Configure the syslog daemon not to store unneeded messages locally
Add a suppression period to the analytics rules
Move the connector to Windows Forwarded Events
questions.explain: Microsoft advises configuring the daemon not to keep unneeded logs, because a full disk stops the AMA. Event sets apply to Windows Security events. Forwarded Events is Windows-only. Rule suppression doesn't affect ingestion.

questions.stem: A firewall sends Common Event Format messages through CEF via AMA. In which table should analysts query the parsed events?
questions.explain: CEF via AMA parses CEF into CommonSecurityLog (DeviceVendor, SourceIP, Activity…). Syslog holds plain syslog, SecurityEvent holds Windows Security events, and AzureDiagnostics holds some Azure resource logs.

questions.case: One Linux forwarder has both a Syslog via AMA DCR and a CEF via AMA DCR collecting facility local4. A proxy appliance sends CEF on local4, and its vendor doesn't allow the facility to be changed. Finance notices the proxy's events are billed twice.
questions.stem: What should you do?
options: Add a transformation to the Syslog DCR that drops messages containing CEF
Set the Syslog DCR minimum level for local4 to LOG_EMERG
Move CommonSecurityLog to the Auxiliary plan
Delete the CEF via AMA DCR and parse CEF from the Syslog table
questions.explain: When the device facility can't change, Microsoft's fix is an ingestion-time transformation on the Syslog stream that drops CEF records. Dropping the CEF DCR loses parsed CommonSecurityLog data. LOG_EMERG still duplicates emergency messages. Changing the plan doesn't remove duplicates.

questions.stem: You add an ingestion-time transformation to a Syslog DCR so that CEF messages are not duplicated in the Syslog table. Complete the KQL.
questions.code:
source
| where ProcessName !contains "CEF" ____ SyslogMessage !contains "CEF:0"
questions.explain: A record is kept only if neither field shows CEF, so both conditions must hold: 'and'. With 'or', a CEF message flagged in only one field would still be kept. '|' would start an invalid pipe and 'with' isn't a KQL logical operator.

questions.stem: You onboard a Check Point firewall with CEF via AMA using a new Azure VM as the forwarder. Put the steps in order.
options: Install the Common Event Format solution from Content hub
Create a data collection rule on the CEF via AMA connector targeting the forwarder VM
Configure the firewall to send CEF to the forwarder's IP on port 514
Query CommonSecurityLog to verify the events arrive
questions.explain: You install the solution, create the DCR (which also installs the AMA), run the script to set up rsyslog or syslog-ng on 514, point the appliance at the forwarder, then verify in CommonSecurityLog (allow up to about 20 minutes).

questions.stem: You connect the Azure Activity connector with the Azure Policy Assignment wizard at subscription scope. Existing subscriptions never send data, but subscriptions created later do. What did you most likely skip?
options: Installing the AMA on a VM in each subscription
Assigning the Monitoring Metrics Publisher role
questions.explain: deployIfNotExists policies act automatically only on new or updated resources. A remediation task applies the diagnostic setting to existing ones. Monitoring Metrics Publisher is for the Logs Ingestion API. The activity log needs no agent or Defender for Cloud.

questions.stem: Which table stores Azure Activity log events ingested by the Azure Activity connector?
questions.explain: Subscription control-plane events land in AzureActivity. AuditLogs holds Entra ID directory audit events, AzureDiagnostics holds some resource logs, and CloudAppEvents is the Defender for Cloud Apps advanced hunting table.

questions.stem: You are connecting the Azure Activity log for a subscription to Microsoft Sentinel. Put the steps in order.
options: Install the Azure Activity solution from Content hub
Open the connector page and select Launch Azure Policy Assignment wizard
On Basics, select the subscription as the scope
On Parameters, select the Sentinel Log Analytics workspace
On Remediation, select Create a remediation task, then create the assignment
questions.explain: Install the solution, open the connector's policy wizard, set the scope, choose the primary workspace, tick the remediation task so existing resources comply, then review and create.

questions.case: Litware's policy requires Key Vault audit logs from every vault in subscription Prod-01, including vaults teams will create in future. The SOC engineer has Microsoft Sentinel Contributor on the workspace and Reader on Prod-01.
questions.stem: What should the engineer do first?
options: Obtain the Owner role on Prod-01, then run the Key Vault connector's Azure Policy wizard
Deploy the Azure Monitor Agent to each vault
Add a diagnostic setting on each existing vault
Enable the Defender XDR connector and stream CloudAppEvents
questions.explain: Policy-managed connectors need Owner on the assignment scope, and Azure Policy covers both existing (with remediation) and future vaults. Per-vault settings miss new vaults. PaaS resources don't run the AMA. CloudAppEvents doesn't carry Key Vault audit logs.

questions.stem: When using a standalone diagnostic settings-based connector, which destination option do you select in the resource's diagnostic setting?
questions.explain: Sentinel reads from its Log Analytics workspace, so you tick Send to Log Analytics workspace and pick the Sentinel workspace. Storage archive, event hub streaming and partner solutions are valid destinations, but Sentinel doesn't read data from them.

questions.stem: For each statement about diagnostic settings-based connectors, select Yes if true.

statements.s: An Azure Policy-managed connector applies one diagnostic settings configuration to all resources of a type within the chosen scope.
A policy-managed connector shows as connected only if data was ingested within the past 14 days.
Diagnostic settings require the Azure Monitor Agent to be installed on the Azure PaaS resource.

questions.explain: Policy-managed connectors deploy one configuration per resource type across the scope. Their status turns disconnected after 14 days without data. Diagnostic settings are a platform feature, and PaaS resources don't run agents.

questions.stem: You configure the Threat Intelligence – TAXII data connector. Which TWO values must you provide for each collection (besides a friendly name)? Select TWO.
questions.explain: The TAXII connector needs a friendly name, the server's API root URL and the collection ID, plus a username and password only if the server requires them. DCE URIs and Entra app secrets belong to API-based ingestion. Workspace keys belong to the legacy Data Collector API.

questions.stem: Your threat intelligence platform (TIP) must push STIX indicators and threat actor objects to Microsoft Sentinel. Microsoft recommends a method that doesn't need a data connector. What should you use?
questions.explain: The Upload API accepts STIX objects from TIPs at workspace scope with no connector, and its Entra app needs Microsoft Sentinel Contributor. The TIP connector is deprecated and limited to indicators. TAXII is a pull client, so the TIP would need to host a TAXII server. The legacy table no longer receives data.

questions.stem: For each statement about threat intelligence ingestion in Microsoft Sentinel, select Yes if true.

statements.s: The TAXII connector can import from TAXII 2.0 and TAXII 2.1 servers.
A CSV import file can contain threat actor and relationship objects as well as indicators.
New STIX indicators are stored in the ThreatIntelIndicators table.

questions.explain: TAXII import supports 2.0 and 2.1. CSV import handles indicators only, while STIX 2.1 JSON files can carry threat actors, attack patterns, identities and relationships. Indicators are stored in ThreatIntelIndicators, with other objects in ThreatIntelObjects.

questions.case: An analyst writes a new hunting query that joins SigninLogs with the ThreatIntelligenceIndicator table. It returns no matches for indicators added this month, although the indicators appear on the Threat intelligence page.
questions.stem: What should the analyst change?
options: Increase the workspace retention to 2 years
Query ThreatIntelIndicators instead of the legacy table
questions.explain: The legacy ThreatIntelligenceIndicator table stopped receiving data after July 2025. Current indicators live in ThreatIntelIndicators (and other objects in ThreatIntelObjects). Re-importing doesn't change the destination table, and Fusion and retention don't affect it either.

questions.stem: You create a DCR-based custom table with Azure CLI to store data from an HR application. Which naming requirement applies?
options: The name must end with _CL, and you must add it yourself
The name must match the DCR name exactly
The name must start with Custom- and the portal adds it
questions.explain: Custom log tables end in _CL. The portal appends it automatically, but CLI, PowerShell, REST and ARM don't. _CF is for custom columns. 'Custom-' prefixes the DCR stream name, not the table, and the table name is independent of the DCR name.

questions.case: A developer's script sends JSON to a custom table through the Logs Ingestion API. It authenticates with an Entra app registration and gets a 403 Forbidden from the DCR endpoint. The app has Log Analytics Contributor on the workspace.
questions.stem: Which role assignment fixes the problem?
options: Log Analytics Reader on the workspace
Monitoring Metrics Publisher on the data collection rule
Microsoft Sentinel Responder on the workspace
questions.explain: Logs Ingestion API callers need Monitoring Metrics Publisher on the DCR they send to. Workspace roles like Log Analytics Contributor manage tables but don't grant ingestion rights. Sentinel Responder handles incidents, and Monitoring Contributor manages monitoring settings rather than publishing data.

questions.stem: Your sample JSON has a string field named EventTime but no TimeGenerated column. Complete the DCR transformation so every record gets a valid TimeGenerated.
questions.code:
source
| extend TimeGenerated = ____(EventTime)
questions.explain: TimeGenerated must be a datetime, so todatetime() converts the string. tostring keeps it a string, format_datetime formats a datetime as text, and bin() rounds values into buckets, which needs a datetime or number input anyway.

questions.stem: For each statement about custom log tables, select Yes if true.

statements.s: When you create a custom table in the portal, a sample JSON file is used to define the table schema.
For Custom Logs via AMA, the destination table must be created before you create the DCR.
Custom tables can only use the Analytics table plan.

questions.explain: The portal infers the schema from a sample file. Custom Logs via AMA needs the _CL table (TimeGenerated plus RawData) first. Custom tables can use Analytics, Basic or Auxiliary/data lake plans.

questions.stem: A custom detection rule queries the DeviceProcessEvents table. Which THREE columns must the query results include? Select THREE.
questions.explain: Defender for Endpoint tables need Timestamp (or TimeGenerated), DeviceId and ReportId so alerts link back to events. A SHA256 column is only needed for file actions such as quarantine. AlertId belongs to alert tables and isn't required.

questions.stem: Your detection counts antivirus detections per device. Complete the query so it keeps the columns a custom detection rule requires.
questions.code:
DeviceEvents
| where ActionType == "AntivirusDetection"
| summarize (Timestamp, ReportId) = ____(Timestamp, ReportId), count() by DeviceId
| where count_ > 5
questions.explain: arg_max(Timestamp, ReportId) returns the latest event's Timestamp and its matching ReportId. make_set returns arrays and dcount returns a number. take_any returns arbitrary values that may not come from the latest event.

questions.stem: You set a custom detection rule on Defender XDR data to run every 3 hours. What lookback period does each run use?
questions.explain: Lookbacks for Defender data are fixed: hourly rules look back 4 hours, 3-hourly 12 hours, 12-hourly 48 hours and daily 30 days. The longer lookback catches late-arriving events, and duplicate alerts are grouped.

questions.case: A hunter wants a custom detection that fires within minutes when an Office process spawns powershell.exe. Her query joins DeviceProcessEvents to DeviceNetworkEvents to add the remote IP, and she wants the Continuous (NRT) frequency.
questions.stem: What must she change to save the rule with Continuous frequency?
options: Change the scope to all device groups
Map the remote IP as an impacted asset
Remove the join so the query references only one table
Add a where Timestamp > ago(1h) filter
