questions.explain: Continuous (NRT) custom detections must reference one table, with no joins, unions or externaldata. Adding a Timestamp filter is discouraged, because the service applies the lookback itself. Scope doesn't affect NRT eligibility, and IP is evidence, not an impacted asset.

questions.stem: For each statement about custom detection rules in Defender XDR, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Every 6 hours is one of the frequency options for rules on Defender XDR data.
Each rule run can generate at most 150 alerts.
When saved, a new rule immediately checks the past 30 days of data.

questions.explain: The options are Continuous (NRT), every 1, 3, 12 or 24 hours, and Custom for Sentinel data only. There is no 6-hour option. Each run is capped at 150 alerts, and a new rule first scans 30 days of data.

questions.stem: Following least privilege, which Microsoft Defender permission lets an analyst create custom detection rules on Microsoft Defender XDR data?
questions.explain: The Defender permission Security settings (manage) is enough to manage custom detections. Global Administrator works but is excessive. Security Reader and Sentinel Reader are read-only. Rules on Sentinel data also need Microsoft Sentinel Contributor.

questions.stem: A custom detection should automatically soft-delete phishing messages found by the query. Which columns must the query output for this action?
questions.explain: Email actions (move to folder, soft or hard delete) need NetworkMessageId and RecipientEmailAddress to find each copy of the message. Sender and Subject don't identify a specific mailbox copy. DeviceId is for device actions, and InternetMessageId isn't the key the action uses.

questions.stem: Which TWO actions can a custom detection rule take automatically against devices returned by the query? Select TWO.
options: Offboard device from Defender for Endpoint
questions.explain: Device actions are isolate, collect investigation package, run antivirus scan, initiate investigation and restrict app execution. Live response is an interactive session. Offboarding and reimaging aren't available as custom detection actions.

questions.stem: What happens when a custom detection rule runs the 'Mark user as compromised' action?
options: The user's Microsoft Entra ID risk level is set to high
The user's password is reset immediately
The user is added to a Defender XDR watchlist
The user's account is disabled in Active Directory
questions.explain: Mark user as compromised raises the user risk level to high in Entra ID Protection, which risk-based Conditional Access can then act on. Disabling and resetting authentication are separate actions that need SID columns. Defender XDR has no watchlist for this.

questions.stem: In the Microsoft Defender portal, where do you manage existing custom detection rules?
questions.explain: Custom detections live under Hunting > Custom detection rules, alongside Sentinel analytics rules when a workspace is onboarded. Indicators are IoC allow/block entries, Tune alert creates suppression or tuning rules, and Device groups manage RBAC scoping.

questions.stem: A custom detection is producing false positives while you rework its logic. You want it to stop running but keep its configuration for later. What should you do?
options: Select Run to reset the interval
Change its frequency to every 24 hours
questions.explain: Turn off stops the rule without losing it, and you can turn it back on later. Delete removes it permanently. Run executes it immediately, which makes things worse. A 24-hour frequency still fires, and its lookback grows to 30 days.

questions.stem: In a Microsoft Sentinel scheduled analytics rule, what is the allowed range for both 'Run query every' and 'Lookup data from the last'?
questions.explain: Both settings accept 5 minutes to 14 days, and the interval must not exceed the lookback. One-minute cadence is NRT. 30 days and 7 days are other limits (custom detection lookback, and the alert grouping window).

questions.case: A scheduled rule detects password spray. Each run may return hundreds of matching accounts. Analysts want one incident per affected account, and each account's alerts within a 5-hour window should go into that incident.
questions.stem: Which configuration should you use?
options: Alert per result with alert grouping on matching selected entities (Account)
Suppression for 5 hours with incident creation disabled
Alert per result with incident creation disabled
Group all events into a single alert with grouping of all alerts from the rule
questions.explain: One alert per result plus grouping by the Account entity in a 5-hour window gives one incident per account. A single summary alert merges every account. Suppression and disabling incidents stop the incidents analysts need, and alert-only output is hidden in the Defender portal.

questions.stem: For each statement about scheduled analytics rules, select Yes if true.

statements.s: A rule can include up to 10 entity mappings.
The query interval can be longer than the lookback period to reduce cost.
Suppression can stop the rule from running for up to 24 hours after it generates an alert.

questions.explain: Rules allow up to 10 entity mappings with up to 3 identifiers each. An interval longer than the lookback leaves gaps and fails validation. Suppression is configurable up to 24 hours.

questions.stem: You create a new scheduled query rule in Microsoft Sentinel. Put the wizard tabs in order.
options: Set rule logic (query, entities, schedule, threshold)
questions.explain: The analytics rule wizard runs General → Set rule logic → Incident settings → Automated response → Review + create. Validation on the final tab checks things such as the interval being no longer than the lookback.

questions.stem: You need an alert within about two minutes whenever the Security log is cleared (event 1102) on any server. Which analytics rule type best fits?
options: Scheduled rule running every 5 minutes over 1 hour
questions.explain: NRT rules run every minute with a 2-minute built-in delay, ideal for rare, high-value single events. A 5-minute scheduled rule adds a 5-minute delay. Anomaly rules don't alert. Microsoft Security rules turn alerts from other Microsoft products into incidents.

questions.stem: Which TWO statements describe limits of Microsoft Sentinel NRT rules? Select TWO.
options: NRT rules can query only one workspace and one table
NRT rules can't trigger automation rules
NRT rules cannot use entity mapping
Each run can produce up to 30 single-event alerts
No more than 50 NRT rules can be defined per customer
questions.explain: NRT rules are limited to 50 per customer and up to 30 single-event alerts per run (29 plus a summary alert). They support entity mapping and automation, and they can now query multiple tables and workspaces.

questions.stem: You want alerts when CEF firewall logs show traffic to IP addresses in Microsoft's threat intelligence. You don't want to ingest a full indicator feed or write or maintain a query. What should you enable?
options: Microsoft Defender Threat Intelligence Analytics rule
A TI map IP entity to CommonSecurityLog scheduled rule
questions.explain: The Microsoft Defender Threat Intelligence Analytics rule matches Microsoft indicators against CEF, DNS and Syslog data with no query to maintain. TI map rules match your ingested indicators through an editable query. Fusion correlates alerts, and ML behavior analytics covers SSH and RDP logins.

questions.case: Tailspin onboards its Microsoft Sentinel workspace to the Microsoft Defender portal. Before onboarding, the workspace had the Fusion rule enabled and two Microsoft Security incident creation rules for Defender for Cloud alerts.
questions.stem: For each statement, select Yes if true after onboarding.

statements.s: The Fusion rule is disabled, and Defender XDR correlation creates incidents instead.
The Microsoft Security incident creation rules stay active to avoid losing incidents.
Scheduled analytics rules can still be created and edited with the analytics rule wizard.

questions.explain: Onboarding disables Fusion and deactivates Microsoft Security incident creation rules to avoid duplicates, and the Defender XDR engine handles incident creation and correlation. Scheduled rule creation and management are unchanged.

questions.stem: Your SOC manager asks how much ATT&CK coverage would improve if the team enabled the available rule templates for the Credential Access tactic, before anything is deployed. What should you use?
options: The Analytics page Active rules tab filtered by tactic
Threat analytics reports for Credential Access
The Anomalies table filtered by tactic
Simulated rules on the Sentinel MITRE ATT&CK page
questions.explain: The MITRE ATT&CK page's Simulated rules option shows the coverage you would gain from available detections that aren't configured yet. The Active rules tab shows only deployed rules. The Anomalies table holds ML output, and threat analytics reports don't model your coverage.

questions.stem: For each statement about the MITRE ATT&CK page in Microsoft Sentinel, select Yes if true.

statements.s: By default the matrix counts active scheduled and NRT analytics rules.
Disabled analytics rules are shown as active coverage.
Incidents inherit MITRE techniques from the rules that generated their alerts.

questions.explain: Active coverage counts enabled scheduled and NRT rules. Disabled rules aren't active coverage, though templates can be viewed as simulated coverage. Incidents gain the techniques of the rules behind their alerts.

questions.stem: Where are the results of Microsoft Sentinel anomaly rules stored?
questions.explain: Anomaly rules don't create alerts or incidents. They write to the Anomalies table, which is used for hunting and investigation context. SecurityAlert and SecurityIncident hold alerts and incidents. BehaviorAnalytics is the UEBA enrichment table, not where anomaly rule output goes.

questions.stem: A built-in anomaly rule produces too many anomalies. Put the tuning steps in order.
options: Adjust the threshold and parameters on the '- Customized' copy
Run the copy in Flighting mode and compare results in the Anomalies table
Switch the customized copy to Production
questions.explain: Built-in anomaly rules can't be edited. You duplicate one, tune the copy (which starts in Flighting), compare outputs by AnomalyTemplateId, then promote the copy to Production. The original then switches to Flighting automatically.

questions.case: An analyst tuned a copy of 'Anomalous sign-in location' and wants the copy's improved threshold to become the official version. The original rule is currently in Production.
questions.stem: What happens when the analyst switches the customized copy to Production?
options: Both rules run in Production and results are merged
The original rule automatically switches to Flighting
questions.explain: Only one version of an anomaly rule can be in Production at a time, so promoting the copy flips the original to Flighting. Built-in rules can't be deleted. Anomaly rules never create incidents, only Anomalies table records.

questions.stem: You want to review the past day of output from one anomaly rule to judge whether its threshold is too low. Complete the query.
questions.code:
____
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where RuleId contains "<RuleId>"
questions.explain: Anomaly rule output is in the Anomalies table, filtered by RuleId (expand AnomalyReasons for detail). SecurityAlert holds alerts, which anomalies don't create. BehaviorAnalytics is UEBA enrichment, and IdentityInfo holds identity attributes.

questions.stem: You must remove a delivered phishing message from 40 mailboxes, and users and admins must still be able to recover it later if needed. Which remediation action should you choose?
options: Block the sender in the Tenant Allow/Block List
questions.explain: Soft delete moves the message to Recoverable Items\Deletions, where it can still be recovered. Hard delete purges it. Move to junk leaves it reachable by the user. A Tenant Allow/Block List entry stops future mail but doesn't remove messages already delivered.

questions.stem: Your tenant has Defender for Office 365 Plan 1. Analysts want the Campaigns view, post-delivery email data and Go hunt from the email hunting tool. What do they need?
options: Content search in Microsoft Purview eDiscovery
Threat Explorer, included with Defender for Office 365 Plan 2
Message trace in the Exchange admin center
questions.explain: Threat Explorer (Plan 2) adds the Campaigns and URL clicks views, post-delivery data and Go hunt. Real-time detections, which Plan 1 already has, show only delivery-time detections. Content search and message trace aren't threat-hunting views.

questions.stem: Which TWO locations let an analyst manually start remediation (for example, soft delete) of delivered email in Defender for Office 365 Plan 2? Select TWO.
options: Take actions on advanced hunting results
questions.explain: Both Threat Explorer and advanced hunting offer Take action for email remediation. Attack simulation training runs phishing simulations, Configuration analyzer compares policy settings, and Secure Score tracks posture. None of those remediate delivered mail.

questions.stem: For each statement about Defender for Office 365 remediation, select Yes if true.

statements.s: AIR automated remediation for message clusters can be configured to hard delete messages.
Email remediation actions from the past 30 days can be reviewed on the History tab of the Action center.
With two-step approval, one analyst adds messages to a remediation and another analyst approves it.

questions.explain: Automated remediation of AIR clusters uses soft delete only. The Action center History tab shows the last 30 days of remediation. Two-step approval splits selecting messages from approving the action.

questions.stem: You suspect a compromised mailbox has a forwarding rule that is hidden from Outlook. Complete the Exchange Online PowerShell command so hidden rules are included.
questions.code: Get-InboxRule -Mailbox "megan@contoso.com" ____ | Format-List Name,Enabled,RedirectTo,ForwardTo,ForwardAsAttachmentTo
questions.explain: Get-InboxRule returns hidden inbox rules only when you add -IncludeHidden, and attackers often hide forwarding rules. -ShowHidden, -All and -Force don't reveal hidden rules.

questions.stem: A user's mailbox is confirmed compromised and has been sending fraud emails. Put the response steps in order.
options: Disable the account (or reset the password if you can't disable it)
Revoke the user's active sessions and refresh tokens
Remove persistence: unknown MFA methods, consented apps and malicious forwarding or inbox rules
Re-enable the account and remove it from Restricted entities
questions.explain: First stop the attacker (disable or reset the password), then kill existing sessions so they can't re-add persistence, then remove persistence (MFA methods, apps, inbox rules), and only then restore the user, including unblocking outbound mail on the Restricted entities page.

questions.stem: How can an analyst quickly spot, in the Defender portal incident queue, the incidents where automatic attack disruption has taken action?
options: By the Defender Experts tag on the incident
By the Redirected tag on the incident
By the Attack Disruption tag on the incident
questions.explain: Disrupted incidents carry an Attack Disruption tag, and the incident page also shows a yellow banner. Redirected marks merged source incidents. Defender Experts marks managed-service involvement. 'Multi-stage' is only an automatic name.

questions.stem: You are preparing Defender for Office 365 signals for automatic attack disruption. Which THREE mailbox audit actions are among the minimum that must be enabled? Select THREE.
questions.explain: The documented minimum is MailItemsAccessed, UpdateInboxRules, MoveToDeletedItems, SoftDelete and HardDelete. FolderBind and SendAs are real mailbox audit actions but aren't on that list.

questions.case: During a BEC attack, automatic attack disruption disabled the account of Lee, a finance manager. Your investigation shows that the attacker's sessions were revoked, Lee's password and MFA methods were reset, and no persistence remains. Lee needs access again now.
questions.stem: What should you do?
options: In the incident graph or Action center, select Lee and choose Enable user
Add Lee as a user exclusion under Automated response > Identities
Dismiss Lee's user risk in Microsoft Entra ID Protection
Open a support case titled 'Attack disruption opt-out'
questions.explain: Analysts release disruption actions themselves, using Enable user for an account or release from containment for a device, from the incident graph or the Action center. An exclusion only prevents future actions. Opting out disables the feature for the whole tenant. Dismissing risk doesn't re-enable a disabled account.

questions.stem: For each statement about automatic attack disruption, select Yes if true.

statements.s: To stop a specific service account from being disabled automatically, add it as a user exclusion under Settings > Microsoft Defender XDR > Automated response.
Attack disruption requires Microsoft Defender Antivirus to run in active mode on endpoints.
Microsoft recommends setting Defender for Endpoint device groups to Full automation for attack disruption.

questions.explain: User exclusions are configured on the Identities tab of Automated response. Disruption works whether Defender Antivirus is in active mode, passive mode or EDR block mode. Full - remediate threats automatically is the recommended automation level.

questions.stem: You need an organization-wide list of the automatic attack disruption actions taken in the last 30 days. Complete the advanced hunting query.
questions.code:
____
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| project Timestamp, ActionType, DeviceName, SourceUserName, IpAddress, PolicyName
| order by Timestamp desc
questions.explain: DisruptionAndResponseEvents records automatic attack disruption block and policy events, with columns such as PolicyName and SourceUserName. DeviceEvents can show activity blocked by containment but isn't the org-wide disruption log. AlertEvidence lists alert entities, and EmailPostDeliveryEvents covers email actions.

questions.stem: Your tenant has Microsoft 365 E5. Analysts report that DLP policy matches are never visible in the Defender XDR incident queue. What should you configure in Microsoft Purview?
options: Turn on data sharing with other security solutions in Insider Risk Management settings
Create a Defender for Cloud Apps file policy for each DLP rule
Turn on alerts for the DLP policies
Enable the Microsoft Defender XDR connector in Microsoft Sentinel
questions.explain: Licensed tenants get DLP alerts in Defender automatically, but only for DLP policies that generate alerts, so alerts must be turned on in Purview. The IRM setting affects only insider risk data. The Sentinel connector sends data to Sentinel, not to Defender. File policies are a separate product feature.

questions.stem: A DLP alert in the Defender portal concerns a OneDrive file that contains customer passport numbers. Which THREE remediation actions can you take on that file from the alert? Select THREE.
questions.explain: For SharePoint and OneDrive files, the DLP alert offers apply retention label, apply sensitivity label, unshare, delete and download. Isolate device is a Defender for Endpoint device action, and soft delete applies to email messages.

questions.stem: An analyst can manage DLP alerts in the Defender portal but can't download the file that matched the policy. Which role is missing?
questions.explain: Downloading the matched file from a DLP alert requires the Data classification content viewer role. Security Reader and Security Operator cover alerts, not content. eDiscovery Manager is for eDiscovery cases.

questions.stem: DLP audit activity for SharePoint and OneDrive is queried in advanced hunting. Complete the query with the correct table.
questions.code:
____
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountDisplayName == "Adele Vance"
| project Timestamp, ActionType, Application, ObjectName
questions.explain: DLP audit data from Microsoft 365 apps is in CloudAppEvents, which requires the Microsoft 365 connector in Defender for Cloud Apps. DeviceFileEvents holds endpoint file events, EmailEvents holds mail flow, and IdentityDirectoryEvents holds directory changes.

questions.stem: You want Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management alerts to appear in the Defender XDR incident queue. What should you turn on?
options: The Microsoft 365 app connector in Defender for Cloud Apps
Data sharing with other security solutions in Insider Risk Management settings
Alerts for all DLP policies in Purview
Pseudonymization of usernames in Insider Risk Management
questions.explain: The IRM setting that shares data with other security solutions sends IRM alerts and events to Defender XDR. DLP alert settings and the Defender for Cloud Apps connector feed other data. Pseudonymization only masks names inside IRM.

questions.stem: For each statement about Insider Risk Management data in Defender XDR, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Only users who hold an insider risk analysis or investigation role in Microsoft Purview can view IRM data in Defender XDR.
IRM data in Defender XDR stays pseudonymized, so it can't be correlated with Defender for Endpoint alerts.
IRM data can be queried with advanced hunting in the Defender portal.

questions.explain: IRM data in Defender isn't pseudonymized, so it can correlate with other alerts. Access is limited to IRM analysts and investigators instead. IRM data is available in advanced hunting, Graph and Sentinel.

questions.case: Contoso enabled IRM integration with Defender XDR last month. Priya, the SOC lead, holds the Security Administrator role and can see Defender for Endpoint and Defender for Office 365 alerts. Her colleague in the Purview insider risk team can see an IRM 'data theft by departing user' alert in the Defender incident, but Priya can't.
questions.stem: What is the most likely reason?
options: The Sentinel workspace isn't connected to the Defender portal
IRM alerts are visible only in the Purview portal
Priya isn't assigned an Insider Risk Management analyst or investigator role in Purview
Priya's account has no Security Copilot SCUs assigned
questions.explain: IRM data in Defender XDR is restricted to users with IRM analysis or investigation roles, so Security Administrator isn't enough. Copilot SCUs aren't needed to see alerts. Her colleague can see the alert in Defender, so the alert does reach the portal and Sentinel isn't required.

questions.stem: On a Defender for Cloud alert's Take action tab, which section lists security recommendations that harden the resource and reduce its attack surface?
questions.explain: Prevent future attacks lists hardening recommendations. Mitigate the threat gives manual remediation steps for this alert, Inspect resource context opens activity logs, and Trigger automated response runs a Logic App.

questions.stem: An authorized penetration test runs against one Azure VM for the next three weeks and keeps raising the same Defender for Servers alert. You want matching alerts dismissed automatically only until the test ends. What should you do?
options: Create a suppression rule with a custom expiration date
Create a workflow automation that emails the subscription owner
Disable the Defender for Servers plan on the subscription
Bulk-change the existing alerts to Dismissed each day
questions.explain: Suppression rules dismiss matching future alerts automatically, and a custom expiration ends the rule when the test finishes. Manual dismissal doesn't scale, disabling the plan removes protection, and an email automation doesn't suppress anything.

questions.stem: You must create a Defender for Cloud workflow automation and the Logic App it runs when a high-severity alert fires. Which TWO permissions do you need? Select TWO.
options: Security Admin or Owner on the resource group
questions.explain: Workflow automation needs Security Admin or Owner on the resource group, and creating or editing the Logic App needs Logic App Contributor. Logic App Operator can only run or read existing apps. The reader roles can't create anything.

questions.stem: For each statement about Defender for Cloud alerts in the Defender portal, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Informational-severity Defender for Cloud alerts are sent to the Defender XDR alert queue.
Resolving a Defender for Cloud alert in the Defender portal syncs the status back to Defender for Cloud.
Status changes to a Defender for Endpoint alert on an Azure VM sync between Defender for Cloud and Defender XDR.

questions.explain: Informational alerts aren't sent to Defender XDR. Status syncs both ways for alerts that originate in Defender for Cloud. Defender for Endpoint alerts on cloud resources appear in both portals, but their status doesn't sync.

questions.case: Fabrikam uses Microsoft Sentinel, onboarded to the Defender portal, and ingests Defender XDR incidents. It also enabled the subscription-based Microsoft Defender for Cloud connector years ago, and an analytics rule creates incidents from Defender for Cloud alerts. Analysts now see every cloud alert twice.
questions.stem: What should you do?
options: Add #DONT_CORR# to every analytics rule description
Use the tenant-based Defender for Cloud connector, disconnect the legacy one and turn off the incident-creating rule
Create a Defender for Cloud suppression rule for all alert types
Turn off the Defender for Cloud integration in Defender XDR settings
questions.explain: Microsoft's guidance is to move to the tenant-based connector, disconnect the subscription-based legacy connector and disable the analytics rules that create incidents from Defender for Cloud alerts. #DONT_CORR# only affects correlation. Suppressing everything or removing the integration loses real detections.

questions.stem: You are working a genuine Defender for Cloud alert on a storage account. Put the recommended response steps in order.
options: Follow the Mitigate the threat steps to investigate and contain
Remediate the Prevent future attacks recommendations
Trigger a Logic App for any automated follow-up
Set the alert status to Dismissed when the investigation is complete
questions.explain: Defender for Cloud's recommended order is to mitigate the immediate threat, harden through the recommendations, optionally trigger automation, and dismiss the alert once you have finished.

questions.stem: Which Defender for Cloud Apps governance action raises the user's risk level to high in Microsoft Entra ID Protection so that risk-based policies are enforced?
options: Require user to sign in again
questions.explain: Confirm user compromised sets the user's risk to high in Entra ID Protection. Suspend user blocks sign-in, Require user to sign in again revokes tokens and session cookies, and Notify user only sends an email.

questions.stem: A user's session cookie may have been stolen, but you don't want to block the user from working. You want to invalidate refresh tokens and session cookies so the user must authenticate again everywhere. Which governance action should you use?
options: Require user to sign in again
questions.explain: Require user to sign in again revokes refresh tokens and session cookies without blocking the account. Suspend user blocks sign-in. Confirm user compromised changes Entra risk. Revoke app removes an OAuth app's permissions.

questions.stem: For each statement about Defender for Cloud Apps anomaly alerts, select Yes if true.

statements.s: If an Impossible travel alert was caused by an untagged corporate VPN, dismiss the alert and tag the VPN IP range.
Most anomaly detections need a learning period of about seven days before they alert.
Benign true positive is the classification for detections where the reported activity never actually happened.

questions.explain: Tagging VPN ranges prevents repeat impossible-travel false positives, and most detections learn for about seven days. Benign true positive means the activity was real and suspicious but authorized, such as a pen test. A detection error is a false positive.

questions.case: Defender for Cloud Apps raises 'Suspicious inbox forwarding' for Omar in accounts payable. His mailbox now forwards all mail to an external Gmail address. Omar says he didn't create the rule, and sign-in logs show a sign-in from an unfamiliar country an hour earlier.
questions.stem: Which response is most appropriate?
options: Suspend Omar, reset his password and remove the forwarding rule
Ban the OAuth app named in Omar's most recent consent
Dismiss the alert and tag the sign-in IP address as a corporate range
Apply admin quarantine to the files in Omar's OneDrive
questions.explain: This is a true positive. The documented response is to suspend the user, reset the password and remove the forwarding rule. Dismissing the alert ignores the compromise, no OAuth app is implicated, and quarantining files doesn't stop the mail exfiltration.

questions.stem: Which THREE are user governance actions in Defender for Cloud Apps? Select THREE.
options: Require user to sign in again
questions.explain: Notify user, Suspend user and Require user to sign in again act on users, as does Confirm user compromised. Make private is a file governance action, and Revoke app is an app governance action.

questions.stem: A Defender for Cloud Apps 'Unusual ISP for an OAuth app' alert is confirmed as a true positive. What is the recommended first remediation?
options: Suspend the user who first consented to the app
Revoke all OAuth access tokens for the app and investigate how they were generated
Reset the passwords of all users who use the app
Mark the app as Unsanctioned in Cloud Discovery
questions.explain: For a true positive, revoke the app's OAuth access tokens and then investigate how they were issued. Suspending the consenting user doesn't stop the app's tokens. Unsanctioning a Cloud Discovery app affects shadow-IT traffic, and password resets don't invalidate OAuth app tokens.

questions.stem: Which is the least-privileged Microsoft Entra role that can dismiss user risk in ID Protection?
questions.explain: Security Operator is the least-privileged role that can dismiss user risk. Security Reader is read-only. User Administrator is least-privileged for password resets, and Conditional Access Administrator manages policies.

questions.stem: A risk-based Conditional Access policy targets high user risk. What must a cloud-only user do to remediate their own user risk?
options: Sign in from a familiar device and location
Complete MFA and then perform a secure password change
questions.explain: User risk self-remediation requires MFA followed by a secure password change. MFA alone remediates sign-in risk only. A familiar device or location can auto-dismiss sign-in risk, not user risk. Re-registering MFA doesn't clear user risk.

questions.stem: For each statement about Microsoft Entra ID Protection, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Leaked credentials is a user risk detection that is calculated offline.
The Attacker in the Middle detection is always raised as high risk.
Dismissing a user's risk also forces that user to change their password.

questions.explain: Leaked credentials is an offline user risk detection and is always high. Attacker in the Middle is always high and Microsoft recommends investigating it manually. Dismiss risk clears the risk state without changing the password.

questions.case: Tailspin has hybrid identities synced from on-premises AD. Users flagged with high user risk change their passwords with Ctrl+Alt+Del on domain-joined PCs, but their user risk in Entra ID Protection stays High and Conditional Access keeps blocking them.
questions.stem: What should you configure?
options: Enable password hash sync and turn on 'Allow on-premises password change to reset user risk'
Assign Microsoft Entra ID P1 licenses to all users
Enable self-service password reset for cloud-only accounts
questions.explain: For an on-premises password change to remediate user risk, password hash sync must be on and the ID Protection setting 'Allow on-premises password change to reset user risk' must be enabled. Pass-through authentication, P1 licences or SSPR for cloud-only users don't solve this.

questions.stem: You confirmed a user as compromised in ID Protection, and no risk policy has remediated the account yet. Which THREE follow-up actions does Microsoft recommend? Select THREE.
options: Exclude the user from the user risk policy
Block the user if the attacker could reset the password or complete MFA
questions.explain: Recommended follow-ups are requiring a password change, blocking the user when the attacker could pass MFA or reset the password, revoking refresh tokens and disabling compromised devices. Dismissing risk or excluding the user would weaken protection.

questions.stem: In Microsoft Sentinel, you want a count of high-risk Entra ID Protection detections per user and detection type. Complete the query.
questions.code:
____
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RiskLevel == "high"
| summarize Detections = count() by UserPrincipalName, RiskEventType
questions.explain: AADUserRiskEvents holds individual risk detections, with RiskEventType and RiskLevel. AADRiskyUsers holds each user's aggregate risk state. SigninLogs holds sign-ins (with RiskLevelDuringSignIn), and IdentityLogonEvents is a Defender advanced hunting table.

questions.stem: Defender for Identity reports 'Suspected DCSync attack (replication of directory services)'. Which alert category does this belong to?
questions.explain: DCSync abuses replication to pull password hashes, so it's classed as credential access. Reconnaissance covers enumeration such as LDAP or DNS mapping. Lateral movement covers pass-the-hash and pass-the-ticket. Persistence covers changes such as additions to sensitive groups.

questions.stem: Which TWO Defender for Identity alerts are in the lateral movement category? Select TWO.
questions.explain: Pass-the-hash and overpass-the-hash are lateral movement alerts. DNS network mapping is reconnaissance, honeytoken authentication is credential access, and additions to sensitive groups is persistence and privilege escalation.

questions.stem: You select Disable on an on-premises AD account from its identity page in the Defender portal. Which component carries out the action?
options: The Defender for Endpoint agent on the user's last-used device
The Defender for Identity sensor on an AD FS server
The Defender for Identity sensor on the Microsoft Entra Connect server
The Defender for Identity sensor on a domain controller, using the DC's LocalSystem account
questions.explain: AD remediation runs from a sensor on a domain controller, which by default uses the DC's LocalSystem account. Sensors on Entra Connect, AD FS or AD CS servers don't perform remediation, and the endpoint agent can't disable directory accounts.

questions.stem: For each statement about Defender for Identity response actions, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Force password change is supported for both Active Directory and Microsoft Entra ID accounts.
Mark as compromised applies to Active Directory accounts only.
To run identity response actions in the Defender portal, analysts need the Response (manage) permission in unified RBAC.

questions.explain: Force password change covers AD and Entra ID. Mark as compromised applies to Entra ID, where it marks the linked accounts as compromised. Analysts need a unified RBAC role with Response (manage) before identity actions run.

questions.case: You created a decoy account, svc-backup-old, that no legitimate process uses. Today Defender for Identity raised 'Honeytoken authentication activity' for that account from workstation WS-114. No change ticket explains it.
questions.stem: How should you classify and handle the alert?
options: True positive: investigate WS-114 for compromise and find out who used the account
Informational: the account is a decoy, so no action is needed
Benign true positive: tag WS-114 as a security scanner
False positive: exclude svc-backup-old from detections
questions.explain: A honeytoken should never authenticate, so any use without an explanation is a strong compromise signal. Investigate the source device and user. Calling it benign, excluding the decoy or ignoring it defeats the purpose of having a honeytoken.

questions.stem: You onboard a Microsoft Sentinel workspace to the Defender portal. What happens to the active Microsoft security incident creation rules?
options: They are converted into custom detection rules
They are deactivated to prevent duplicate incidents
They are moved to the secondary workspace
They keep running and create incidents in both portals
questions.explain: Microsoft incident creation rules aren't supported in the Defender portal. They are deactivated on onboarding because Defender XDR already creates and correlates those incidents. They aren't converted or moved.

questions.stem: After onboarding Sentinel to the Defender portal, an automation rule that matches on 'Incident title contains Ransomware' sometimes doesn't fire. What is the recommended fix?
options: Add #INC_CORR# to the automation rule name
Use the incident Description field as the condition
Use the name of the analytics rule that created the alerts, plus tags, as the condition
Change the condition to the Incident provider property
questions.explain: Correlation can rename incidents, so Microsoft recommends conditions based on analytics rule names and tags. The Incident provider condition and the Description field are removed after onboarding. Correlation tags go in analytics rule descriptions, not automation rule names.

questions.stem: For each statement about Microsoft Sentinel in the Defender portal, select Yes if true.

statements.s: With multiple workspaces onboarded, only the primary workspace's alerts are correlated with Defender XDR data.
An incident created manually in Sentinel in the Azure portal syncs to the Defender portal incident queue.
Automation rules with an alert trigger act on Defender XDR alerts unless you use the Enhanced Alert Trigger.

questions.explain: Only the primary workspace correlates with XDR data. Incidents created through the API, a Logic App or manually in the Azure portal don't sync to Defender. Standard alert-trigger automation rules act only on Sentinel alerts, and the Enhanced Alert Trigger extends them to Defender XDR alerts.

questions.case: Your tenant's Incident correlation default setting is on. A noisy custom Sentinel analytics rule for VPN sign-ins keeps getting merged into large multi-stage incidents. The SOC wants this rule's alerts grouped only by the rule's own settings. Other rules must still correlate.
questions.stem: What should you do?
options: Turn off the Incident correlation default setting for the tenant
Move the rule to a secondary workspace
Create an automation rule that closes incidents created by the rule
Add #DONT_CORR# at the start of the analytics rule's description
questions.explain: With correlation on by default, #DONT_CORR# at the start of the description (or Incident correlation set to Disabled in the wizard) excludes just that rule. Turning off the tenant default affects every rule. Moving the rule to a secondary workspace and auto-closing its incidents are indirect workarounds with side effects.

questions.stem: The SecurityIncident table stores a new row each time an incident is updated. Complete the query so it returns only the latest record for each incident.
questions.code:
SecurityIncident
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| summarize ____ by IncidentNumber
| where Status != "Closed"
| project IncidentNumber, Title, Severity, Status, Owner
questions.explain: arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) keeps the row with the newest TimeGenerated and all its columns, giving the current state. arg_min returns the first version. max() returns only the timestamp, so Title and Status would be lost. make_set gives a list of values.

questions.stem: After March 31, 2027, where will Microsoft Sentinel be supported?
options: In both the Azure portal and the Defender portal
Only in the Microsoft Defender portal
Only in the Microsoft Purview portal
questions.explain: Microsoft has announced that after March 31, 2027, Sentinel is no longer supported in the Azure portal and is available only in the Defender portal. Azure portal users are redirected there. Sentinel has never run in the Purview portal.

questions.stem: An incident contains an obfuscated, base64-encoded PowerShell command. Which embedded Security Copilot capability explains what the command does?
questions.explain: Script analysis explains suspicious scripts and command lines. Incident report writes up the incident, device summary describes a device's posture and activity, and the Threat Intelligence Briefing Agent produces threat briefings.

questions.stem: Which THREE are categories of Security Copilot guided responses in the Defender portal? Select THREE.
questions.explain: Guided responses have four categories: Triage, Containment, Investigation and Remediation. Exposure (Exposure Management) and Compliance aren't guided-response categories.

questions.stem: For each statement about the Copilot incident summary in the Defender portal, select Yes if true.

statements.s: By default, a summary is generated automatically when you open an incident.
An incident summary can include indicators of compromise and threat actor names when the data is available.
Copilot can summarize incidents of any size, with no limit on the number of alerts.

questions.explain: Summaries are auto-generated by default (you can switch to severity-based or on-demand generation) and include IoCs and threat actors when available. A single summary covers incidents with up to 100 alerts.

questions.stem: An analyst sees a Copilot containment card recommending 'Isolate device', but the action button is grayed out. What is the most likely cause?
options: The incident summary hasn't been regenerated
Copilot cards are read-only for every user
The organization has used up its monthly Security Compute Units
The analyst's unified RBAC permissions don't allow that response action
questions.explain: Grayed-out guided-response buttons show that the user's unified RBAC permissions don't allow the action. Running out of SCUs stops Copilot from generating content, not individual buttons. Regenerating the summary has no effect, and cards are actionable for users with the right permissions.

questions.case: Your SOC opens about 400 incidents a day, most of them low-severity. Copilot consumption is higher than budgeted, because a summary is generated for every incident an analyst opens. Leads still want automatic summaries for medium and high incidents.
questions.stem: What should you configure?
options: Set Incident Summary generation to Auto-generate by incident severity with a minimum of Medium
Set Incident Summary generation to Generate on demand
Remove the Natural Language to KQL plugin
Disable guided responses for all analysts
questions.explain: Severity-based auto-generation summarizes only incidents at or above the chosen severity, which meets both requirements. On-demand generation drops automatic summaries entirely. Removing the KQL plugin or disabling guided responses doesn't change summary consumption.

questions.stem: Which Security Copilot agent in Defender gives verdicts with a natural-language rationale on emails that users report as phishing?
questions.explain: The Phishing Triage Agent, now part of the Security Alert Triage Agent, triages user-reported phishing alerts. The briefing agent writes threat summaries, the hunting assistant helps write KQL, and Conditional Access optimization is an Entra agent.

questions.stem: You are deploying the Phishing Triage Agent. Which THREE are prerequisites? Select THREE.
options: Security Copilot capacity (provisioned SCUs or included entitlement)
The 'Email reported by user as malware or phish' alert policy turned on
A Microsoft Sentinel workspace connected to the Defender portal
Microsoft Defender for Endpoint Plan 2 on all devices
questions.explain: The agent needs MDO Plan 2, Security Copilot capacity and the user-reported phish alert policy (with reporting enabled in Outlook and unified RBAC for MDO). Defender for Endpoint and a Sentinel workspace aren't listed prerequisites.

questions.case: You enabled the Phishing Triage Agent a week ago, but its Performance tab shows no triaged alerts. Users are reporting phish in Outlook, and those alerts appear in the queue already marked Resolved, with no Agent tag.
questions.stem: What should you do?
options: Increase the incident summary minimum severity
Assign the agent identity the Global Administrator role
Disable the built-in 'Auto-Resolve - Email reported by user as malware or phish' tuning rule
Turn on AIR automated remediation for similar URL clusters
questions.explain: Alerts resolved by tuning rules are never sent to the agent, so you must disable the auto-resolve rule and any custom equivalents. Global Administrator contradicts least privilege and isn't required. AIR remediation and summary settings don't affect triage.

questions.stem: For each statement about Security Copilot agents in Defender, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Microsoft recommends running the Phishing Triage Agent with a new Microsoft Entra Agent ID instead of an existing user account.
When the Phishing Triage Agent finds a true positive, it resolves the alert automatically.
Analyst feedback becomes a lesson for the agent only when 'Use this feedback to teach the agent' is selected.

questions.explain: A dedicated Entra Agent ID is recommended because it gets only the permissions the agent needs. The agent resolves false positives and leaves true-positive incidents open for analysts. Feedback without the teach option is kept for audit only.

questions.stem: The Phishing Triage Agent wrongly classified an email. Put the steps in order to correct it and teach the agent.
options: Open the agent card on the incident and select Change classification
Choose the correct classification and explain the reason in plain language
Select 'Use this feedback to teach the agent'
Select Evaluate feedback to preview how it is interpreted
Select Save to store the lesson in the agent's memory
questions.explain: Feedback starts on the agent card with Change classification. You then set the classification and give a reason, select the teach option, evaluate how the agent interprets it, and save it so it becomes a lesson.

questions.stem: Which TWO conditions prevent Defender XDR from automatically merging two related incidents? Select TWO.
options: One of the incidents has a custom tag
The incidents contain alerts from different products
One of the incidents is closed
The incidents are assigned to two different analysts
questions.explain: Automatic merge is blocked when an incident is closed, when the incidents have different assignees, when classifications or determinations differ, and in some device-group cases. Different severities, cross-product alerts and custom tags don't block a merge. Cross-product correlation is the whole point.

questions.stem: After Defender XDR merges incident 512 into incident 498, what happens to incident 512?
options: It is renamed to match 498, and both stay open
It is deleted, along with its alerts
It stays active and is linked to 498 as a child incident
It is closed and tagged Redirected, and its alerts move to 498
questions.explain: Merging moves alerts, tags and entities into the target, closes the source incident and tags it Redirected, so references to it point to the target. There are no parent/child incidents, nothing is deleted, and the source doesn't stay open.

questions.stem: One incident combines alerts from Defender for Office 365, Microsoft Entra ID Protection, and Defender for Cloud Apps. Put the stages of this multi-domain attack in the order they most likely happened.
options: AiTM phishing email delivered and clicked (Defender for Office 365)
Session token replayed from a new location (Entra ID Protection: Anomalous token)
Suspicious inbox forwarding rule created (Defender for Cloud Apps)
Fraudulent payment request sent from the compromised mailbox (BEC financial fraud)
questions.explain: Following the attack story in time order: the phishing click comes first, then the stolen token is replayed, then the attacker hides replies with a mailbox rule, and finally sends the fraud request. Replaying the incident graph chronologically shows this progression.

questions.stem: In a multi-stage incident, you want to see which critical assets an attacker could reach next from a compromised server. Which incident graph feature should you use?
options: Investigation graph in the Investigations tab
questions.explain: Blast radius shows possible propagation paths from a selected node to critical targets. Go hunt runs queries on an entity. Similar incidents lists related incidents, and the Investigations tab shows automated investigation results.

questions.stem: During a lateral movement investigation, you want every alert that involved the compromised account svc-sql in the last 7 days. Complete the advanced hunting query.
questions.code:
AlertEvidence
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where EntityType == "User" and AccountName =~ "svc-sql"
| join kind=inner (AlertInfo) on ____
| project Timestamp, Title, Category, ServiceSource, DeviceName
questions.explain: AlertEvidence and AlertInfo share the AlertId column, which links each evidence row to its alert's title and category. DeviceId and ReportId are columns in device tables, and AlertInfo has no IncidentId column.

questions.stem: What status does a new incident have in the Defender XDR incident queue?
questions.explain: Defender XDR incidents start as Active, and you can then set them to In progress or Resolved. New is the default in Sentinel (Azure portal) and in case management, and Open is a case management status.

questions.stem: A scheduled red-team exercise triggered several credential-theft alerts. You have confirmed the activity was authorized. How should you classify the incident?
options: True positive, with a threat type
Informational, expected activity, with the security testing activity type
questions.explain: Authorized security testing is real activity that was expected, so use Informational, expected activity. False positive means the detection was wrong, which it wasn't. True positive implies a real threat. Not set leaves the incident unclassified.

questions.stem: For each statement about managing Defender XDR incidents, select Yes if true.

statements.s: An incident's default severity is the highest severity of its alerts.
An incident can be assigned to several users at the same time.
Assigning an incident owner also assigns its associated alerts to that owner.

questions.explain: Severity defaults to the highest alert severity and can be changed. Only one user or group can own an incident, and assigning it also assigns all its alerts.

questions.stem: Where can you see who changed an incident's severity, which automation rule added a tag, and when comments were posted?
options: The Microsoft Purview audit log search
questions.explain: The incident Activities log records every manual and automated change, along with comments. The Action center tracks remediation actions, Purview Audit is a tenant-wide search, and Evidence and Response lists entities and their verdicts.

questions.stem: What is required before you can use case management in the Microsoft Defender portal?
options: A Microsoft Sentinel workspace connected to the Defender portal
A ServiceNow connector configured in Defender XDR
questions.explain: Case management requires a Sentinel workspace connected to the Defender portal. It's native, so no ServiceNow connector is needed. Defender Threat Intelligence Projects are deprecated in favour of cases, and Defender Experts is a managed service.

questions.stem: Using Microsoft Sentinel roles, which is the least-privileged role that lets an analyst create cases, assign tasks and link incidents, but not customize case statuses?
questions.explain: Sentinel Responder can create and manage cases and tasks and link incidents. Reader can only view, and Contributor is required to customize statuses. Playbook Operator only runs playbooks.

questions.stem: For each statement about Defender portal case management, select Yes if true.

statements.s: A case can link multiple incidents and threat intelligence indicators.
Cases created in the Defender portal are also visible in Microsoft Sentinel in the Azure portal.
Files attached to a case are scanned for malware before others can download them.

questions.explain: Cases link incidents and, in preview, TI indicators. Cases are visible only in the Defender portal. Attachments are scanned for malware in the background, and Microsoft advises password-zipping samples before uploading.

questions.case: A threat-hunting team tracks a suspected threat actor over several weeks. Its work spans four existing incidents and a dozen IoCs. The team wants its own workflow stages, Research phase and Generating hypothesis, and assigned work items with due dates. It doesn't want a third-party ticketing tool.
questions.stem: Which TWO actions meet these requirements? Select TWO.
options: Have a user with Core security settings (manage) create custom case statuses
Create a Defender Threat Intelligence Project for the actor
Merge the four incidents into one and use incident tags as workflow stages
Create a Sentinel watchlist to track task due dates
Create a case, link the four incidents and the indicators, and add tasks with owners and due dates
questions.explain: A case groups the incidents and IoCs and holds tasks with owners and due dates. Custom statuses, which need Core security settings (manage) or Sentinel Contributor, provide the workflow stages. Merging loses each incident's separate handling. TI Projects are deprecated, and watchlists aren't task trackers.

questions.stem: You open the Timeline tab for a device in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint without changing any settings. Which time range of events is shown by default?
questions.explain: The device timeline shows the past 30 days by default; you change it with the date range picker or the calendar icon. Seven days is the maximum range for one export, not the default view. 90 or 180 days relate to data retention settings, not the default timeline view.

questions.case: An external forensics firm asks for every timeline event from a compromised workstation covering 1 to 10 October. You plan to use the Export option on the device timeline.
questions.stem: What should you expect?
options: One export covers the whole range because exports allow up to 30 days
You need at least two exports because one export covers a maximum of seven days
Only flagged events can be exported, so flag every event first
Export is unavailable; you must use the investigation package instead
questions.explain: The device timeline exports the current date or a specified range of up to seven days, so a 10-day window needs two exports (or use advanced hunting). Export is not limited to flagged events, and the investigation package is a different forensic collection, not a timeline export.

questions.stem: Which actions can you perform directly from the device timeline in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint? Select THREE.
options: Flag events and then filter the timeline to show only flagged events
Delete a timeline event that you have confirmed is a false positive
Select Hunt for related events to open advanced hunting around a selected event
Change the Data type filter to show MITRE ATT&CK techniques
Extend the device's data retention to two years
questions.explain: The timeline supports flagging and a Flagged events filter, Hunt for related events from the event details panel, and a Data type filter for events or techniques. Timeline events are sensor data and cannot be deleted, and data retention is a tenant setting, not a timeline action.

questions.stem: For each statement about the device timeline, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: Timeline entries mapped to MITRE ATT&CK techniques appear in bold with a blue icon, with the technique ID under Additional information.
Running Hunt for related events from a technique side pane returns the technique itself in the results.
Windows Firewall events such as 5157 (blocked connection) appear only when the Audit Filtering Platform Connection policy is enabled.

questions.explain: Techniques are shown bold with a blue icon and their ATT&CK ID and name as tags. Hunting from a technique returns related events but not the technique itself. Firewall events 5025, 5031 and 5157 require the Audit Filtering Platform Connection audit policy.

questions.stem: The timeline shows suspicious activity on device fin-ws-07 between 09:00 and 10:00 UTC. You want a table of only the time, parent process, process name and command line for that hour. Complete the advanced hunting query.
questions.code:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where DeviceName == "fin-ws-07"
| where Timestamp between (datetime(2026-10-14T09:00:00Z) .. datetime(2026-10-14T10:00:00Z))
| ____ Timestamp, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp asc
questions.explain: project keeps only the listed columns, which is what you need before ordering by Timestamp. summarize needs an aggregation function, extend adds calculated columns while keeping all existing ones, and render draws a chart rather than selecting columns.

questions.stem: Which Microsoft Defender for Endpoint device action applies a code integrity policy so that only files signed by Microsoft can run?
questions.explain: Restrict app execution applies a code integrity policy that allows only Microsoft-signed files to run. Isolate device cuts network access, Contain device makes other onboarded devices block an unmanaged device, and Run antivirus scan performs a Quick or Full scan.

questions.stem: A Windows 11 laptop is compromised. You must cut it off from the network immediately but still be able to message and call the user during the investigation. What should you do?
options: Restrict app execution on the device
Isolate the device using full isolation
Isolate the device using selective isolation
questions.explain: Selective isolation (Windows 10 1709 or later and Windows 11) isolates the device but keeps Outlook and Microsoft Teams connected. Full isolation blocks those apps too. Contain device is for unmanaged devices, and Restrict app execution does not block network traffic.

questions.case: Device discovery found a Windows Server 2019 machine in a branch office that was never onboarded to Defender for Endpoint. Alerts show an attacker using it to move laterally to onboarded workstations over SMB. Onboarding the server will take days.
questions.stem: Which action should you take to stop onboarded devices from communicating with the server?
options: Collect an investigation package from the server
Restrict app execution on the server
questions.explain: Contain device is designed for discovered, non-onboarded devices: every onboarded device blocks inbound and outbound communication with it. Isolate, investigation package and Restrict app execution all run through the Defender sensor on the target, which this unmanaged server does not have.

questions.stem: You collect an investigation package from a Windows device. Which items does the package contain? Select THREE.
options: A full memory (RAM) image of the device
Autoruns: registry contents of auto-start entry points
Copies of every user's Documents folder
questions.explain: The Windows investigation package includes Autoruns, installed programs, network connection data, Prefetch files, processes, scheduled tasks, the Security event log, services, SMB sessions, temp directory listings and users and groups. It does not capture a memory image or copy users' documents.

questions.stem: For each statement about device response actions, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: Defender for Endpoint Plan 1 includes the manual Isolate device and Run antivirus scan actions.
Restrict app execution is supported on Windows Server 2012 R2.
When you run an antivirus scan from the device page, you choose between a Quick scan and a Full scan.

questions.explain: Plan 1 includes Run antivirus scan, Isolate device, Stop and quarantine a file and file indicators. Restrict app execution needs Windows 10 1709 or later, Windows 11 or Windows Server 2019 or later. The antivirus scan action offers Quick or Full.

questions.stem: You need to isolate a compromised device in the Microsoft Defender portal and confirm the action worked. Put the steps in order.
options: Open the device page from the alert or device inventory
Select Isolate device on the action bar
Choose full or selective isolation and enter a comment
Select Confirm to submit the action
Check the action status in the Action center
questions.explain: You start on the device page, choose Isolate device, pick the isolation type and add the required comment, confirm, and then verify success in the Action center, which records who submitted the action and whether it succeeded.

questions.stem: During a live response session, which command copies a tool from the live response library onto the device?
questions.explain: putfile places a library file on the device (deleted on restart unless you use -keep). getfile downloads a file from the device to you, run executes a library script, and fileinfo only shows information about a file.

questions.case: An analyst can start live response sessions and successfully runs processes, registry and getfile. When she tries run cleanup.ps1, the command is unavailable. The script is signed and already uploaded to the live response library.
questions.stem: What is the most likely cause?
options: Live response unsigned script execution is turned off
The device must be isolated before scripts can run
Live response for servers is turned off
Her RBAC role grants basic live response but not advanced live response
questions.explain: run is an advanced command, available only to roles with advanced live response permission. The script is signed, so the unsigned-script setting does not matter. Isolation is not required, and live response for servers would block the session entirely, not just one command.

questions.stem: In a live response session you need to run the library script collect-logs.ps1 and pass it the argument -Days 3. Complete the command.
questions.code: run collect-logs.ps1 ____ "-Days 3"
questions.explain: run uses -parameters to pass arguments to a library script. -keep and -overwrite are putfile options (keep after restart, replace an existing file), and -auto runs prerequisite commands for commands such as getfile.

questions.stem: For each statement about live response, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: A live response session is closed after 30 minutes of inactivity.
Two analysts can each hold their own live response session on the same device at the same time.
Pressing Ctrl+C in the portal guarantees that a running remediate command stops on the device.

questions.explain: Inactive sessions time out after 30 minutes. Only one session per device is allowed at a time (a user can have up to five sessions across devices). Ctrl+C cancels the command only in the portal; the agent may continue running operations such as remediate.

questions.stem: You must run an in-house unsigned PowerShell script through live response on a Windows Server 2022 file server. Which settings must be enabled on the Advanced features page? Select THREE.
questions.explain: Live response must be on, servers need the separate Live response for servers toggle, and unsigned PowerShell scripts need Live response unsigned script execution. Tamper protection and automatic alert resolution do not control live response. The analyst still needs advanced live response permission and the script in the library.

questions.stem: On the Evidence and Response tab of a Microsoft Defender XDR incident, which verdicts can be assigned to an analyzed entity?
questions.explain: Each evidence item is marked Malicious, Suspicious or Clean, alongside a remediation status. True positive and False positive are alert classifications, High/Medium/Low are severities, and Active/In progress/Resolved are incident or alert statuses.

questions.stem: On an incident's Evidence and Response tab, a malicious file has the remediation status Pending approval. What can you do from that tab?
options: Change the file's verdict to Clean so the incident closes automatically
Approve or reject the pending remediation action
Submit the file to the live response library
Assign the file to a different incident
questions.explain: For entities with Pending approval, you can approve or reject the remediation action, open the entity, or go hunt from Evidence and Response. Verdicts are not edited to close incidents, and the live response library and incident assignment are unrelated to this tab.

questions.stem: For each statement about the incident page, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: The Assets tab groups the devices, users, mailboxes, apps and cloud resources involved in the incident.
Evidence and Response lists entities such as files, processes, IP addresses and emails analyzed from the incident's alerts.
Rejecting a pending action on Evidence and Response deletes the related alert.

questions.explain: Assets shows Devices, Users, Mailboxes, Apps and Cloud resources. Evidence and Response lists analyzed entities with verdicts and remediation status. Rejecting an action only declines that remediation; it does not delete alerts.

questions.stem: A malicious executable is running on 40 Windows 11 devices and was first seen yesterday. You need to stop its processes, quarantine it and remove its persistence on those devices now. What should you use?
questions.explain: Stop and quarantine file stops running processes, quarantines the file and deletes persistent data such as registry keys on devices that saw it in the last 30 days (up to 1,000 devices). Deep analysis and Download file are for analysis, and an investigation package only collects forensics.

questions.case: A malicious DLL has been observed on 3,500 devices. Many laptops are offline for the next two weeks. Management wants the file blocked everywhere, including when those laptops reconnect.
questions.stem: What is the best response?
options: Run Stop and quarantine file from the file page
Create a file indicator to block the file by its hash
Submit the file for deep analysis
Run a Full antivirus scan on every device
questions.explain: Stop and quarantine is limited to 1,000 devices and times out for devices offline longer than 3 days. A file (hash) indicator blocks the PE file across onboarded devices persistently. Deep analysis only analyzes behavior, and a scan depends on existing detections.

questions.stem: Which statements about deep analysis of a file in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint are true? Select TWO.
options: It runs the file on the original device and records its behavior
It reports behaviors such as contacted IP addresses, dropped files and registry changes
It supports Office documents such as .docx and .xlsx
It runs the file in a secure cloud sandbox and supports PE files such as .exe and .dll
questions.explain: Deep analysis detonates PE files (.exe, .dll) in a Microsoft cloud sandbox and returns observed behaviors like contacted IPs, dropped files and registry changes. It does not execute on the original device, and non-PE files such as Office documents are not supported.

questions.stem: For each statement about the IP address view in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: The list of devices that communicated with the IP address is limited to 100 devices.
Searching an IP returns results even if no device in your organization ever communicated with it.
IP prevalence in the organization is filtered to the past 30 days by default.

questions.explain: The IP activity list shows up to 100 devices with their last event. Searches return results only for IPs that devices in your organization communicated with. Prevalence uses a selectable period that defaults to 30 days.

questions.stem: How can an analyst recognize, in the incident queue, incidents where automatic attack disruption took action?
options: The incident severity is automatically raised to Critical
The incident status is set to Redirected
The incident is assigned to the Microsoft Threat Experts group
The incident shows an Attack Disruption tag
questions.explain: Disrupted incidents show an Attack Disruption tag in the queue and on the incident page, plus a banner describing the automatic action. Disruption does not change severity to Critical, set a Redirected status, or reassign the incident.

questions.stem: Automatic attack disruption never applies the Contain device action in your tenant, although other disruption actions work. Which Defender for Endpoint setting should you check first?
options: Device discovery is set to Standard discovery
Network protection is in block mode
Live response for servers is enabled
questions.explain: The automatic Contain device action requires device discovery set to Standard discovery. Network protection, tamper protection and live response for servers are useful settings but are not the prerequisite for disruption's contain device action.

questions.case: Automatic attack disruption contained a file server and a user account during a ransomware incident. Your investigation is complete: the server is reimaged and the user's password was reset.
questions.stem: Which methods can you use to release the contained assets? Select TWO.
options: On the incident page, select the contained device and choose Release from containment, and select the user and choose Enable user
Open the action in the Action center and undo it from the action details pane
Delete the incident so that all automatic actions are rolled back
Restart the file server to clear the containment policy
questions.explain: Disruption actions are undone from the incident page (Release from containment, Enable user) or from the action details pane in the Action center. Deleting an incident does not roll back actions, and a restart does not remove a containment policy that other onboarded devices enforce.

questions.stem: For each statement about automatic attack disruption, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: The Contain user action disables the account in Microsoft Entra ID.
Defender for Identity disables on-premises AD accounts through its sensor on a domain controller, using the LocalSystem account by default.
Automatic attack disruption works whether Microsoft Defender Antivirus is in active mode, passive mode or EDR block mode.

questions.explain: Contain user blocks the account's network logons on onboarded devices but does not disable it in the identity provider. Disable user in AD runs through the Defender for Identity sensor on the DC, impersonating LocalSystem by default. Disruption works regardless of Defender Antivirus state.

questions.stem: You want to list every automatic attack disruption action taken for incident 4821 during the last 30 days. Complete the advanced hunting query.
questions.code:
____
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where IncidentId == 4821
| project Timestamp, ActionType, AttackDisruptionCategory, DeviceName, AccountUpn
| order by Timestamp desc
questions.explain: DisruptionAndResponseEvents records disruption and response actions across the organization, including IncidentId and AttackDisruptionCategory. DeviceEvents holds block events caused by containment, not the actions themselves; AlertEvidence lists alert entities; IdentityDirectoryEvents shows directory changes such as account disables.

questions.stem: Your organization uses Microsoft Purview Audit (Standard) with no custom retention. How long are audit records retained by default?
questions.explain: Audit (Standard) retains audit records for 180 days. One year is the Audit (Premium) default for Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive and Entra ID records, 10 years requires the add-on license, and 90 days applied only to logs generated before October 2023.

questions.stem: A SOC analyst must be able to search the audit log in the Microsoft Purview portal but must not change any audit configuration. Which role should you assign, following least privilege?
questions.explain: View-Only Audit Logs allows searching and viewing the audit log without configuration rights. Audit Logs also permits managing audit settings, eDiscovery Manager is for eDiscovery cases, and Compliance Administrator is far broader than needed.

questions.stem: You suspect a compromised account created a mailbox rule to forward mail. Complete the Exchange Online PowerShell command to find inbox rules created by megan@contoso.com in the last 14 days.
questions.code: Search-UnifiedAuditLog -StartDate (Get-Date).AddDays(-14) -EndDate (Get-Date) -UserIds megan@contoso.com ____ New-InboxRule -ResultSize 5000
questions.explain: -Operations filters by the operation name, such as New-InboxRule. -RecordType filters by workload record type (not an operation), -FreeText does a text match, and -ObjectIds filters by the target object such as a SharePoint URL.

questions.stem: For each statement about audit log search in the Microsoft Purview portal, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: A search job keeps running if you close the browser.
An activity performed five minutes ago is guaranteed to appear in search results.
With Audit (Standard), you can export up to 50,000 rows from a search.

questions.explain: Audit searches run as jobs that continue after you close the browser and are kept for 30 days. Records from core services typically take 60 to 90 minutes to become available. The export limit is 50,000 rows for Standard and 1,000,000 for Premium.

questions.case: A script runs Search-UnifiedAuditLog for a seven-day window to export all FileDownloaded events for an investigation. It always returns exactly 100 records, although you know there are about 30,000.
questions.stem: What should you change to retrieve all the records with this cmdlet?
options: Add -Formatted so that AuditData is expanded
Use the same -SessionId with -SessionCommand ReturnLargeSet and repeat the call until no results return
Switch to Security & Compliance PowerShell, which has no result limit
questions.explain: Without -SessionCommand the cmdlet returns up to 100 records. ReturnLargeSet with a reused SessionId pages through up to 50,000 results (each call up to -ResultSize 5000). -ResultSize cannot exceed 5,000, -Formatted only changes display, and the cmdlet runs in Exchange Online PowerShell.

questions.stem: Which Microsoft Purview Audit (Premium) event records the search terms a user entered in Outlook?
questions.explain: SearchQueryInitiatedExchange logs searches in Exchange Online mailboxes (for example in Outlook). SearchQueryInitiatedSharePoint covers SharePoint searches, Send covers sent, replied and forwarded mail, and MailItemsAccessed records reads of mail items.

questions.stem: Users have E5 licenses with Advanced Auditing enabled, but no SearchQueryInitiatedExchange events appear for user lee@contoso.com. Complete the command that enables them.
questions.code: Set-Mailbox lee@contoso.com ____ @{Add="SearchQueryInitiated"}
questions.explain: SearchQueryInitiated is added to the mailbox owner audit actions with -AuditOwner. -AuditAdmin and -AuditDelegate set actions logged for admins and delegates, and -AuditLogAgeLimit sets how long mailbox audit entries are kept, not which actions are logged.

questions.case: An attacker signed in to a finance mailbox from 203.0.113.50. MailItemsAccessed records from that IP and session include several Bind entries in Inbox and one Sync entry for the folder Invoices.
questions.stem: How should you scope the data exposure?
options: Treat only the Bind messages as accessed; Sync records are background activity and can be ignored
Treat the Bind messages, identified by InternetMessageId, and every item in the Invoices folder as accessed
Treat the entire mailbox as accessed because any MailItemsAccessed record means full compromise
Treat nothing as accessed until a Send event confirms exfiltration
questions.explain: A Bind record identifies an individual message by InternetMessageId. A Sync record covers a whole folder, so all items in that synced folder are assumed accessed. One folder sync does not by itself prove the whole mailbox was read, and data exposure does not depend on a Send event.

questions.stem: Which capabilities require Microsoft Purview Audit (Premium) rather than Audit (Standard)? Select THREE.
options: Searching the audit log with Search-UnifiedAuditLog
Logging Send events for mail users send, reply to or forward
Exporting search results to a CSV file
Retaining Exchange audit records for one year by default
Retaining audit records for 10 years with the add-on license
questions.explain: Send and other intelligent insights, the one-year default retention for Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive and Entra ID records, and 10-year retention (with the add-on) are Premium features. Both tiers support Search-UnifiedAuditLog and exporting results to CSV.

questions.stem: In March you create a 10-year audit log retention policy for executives who already have the 10-Year Audit Log Retention add-on. Which records will the policy keep for 10 years?
options: Records generated after the policy was created
All records still in the audit log, including those from January
Only records from non-user entities such as service principals
Only records that match a sensitivity label
questions.explain: Audit retention policies are not retroactive: they apply only to records generated after the policy is created. Records from non-user entities are kept for a fixed one year and are not affected by custom policies, and policies are not scoped by sensitivity labels.

questions.stem: In the current Microsoft Purview portal, where do you run a Content search to find every copy of a phishing email across all mailboxes?
options: In Microsoft Purview Audit, as a new search job
In Data lifecycle management, under retention labels
In Communication Compliance, as a new policy
In Microsoft Purview eDiscovery, as a search within a case
questions.explain: Content search functionality now lives in the new eDiscovery experience: you create a search in a case, including the system-generated Content Search case. Audit searches activity records, not message content; retention labels and Communication Compliance policies are not ad hoc content searches.

questions.stem: You need a KeyQL query that returns email items whose subject contains the exact phrase "Payroll update" and that were not sent by hr@contoso.com. Complete the query.
questions.code: kind:email AND subject:"Payroll update" AND ____ from:hr@contoso.com
